examples.translation: Comme le post-traitement corrige les retournements de bits locaux, il compense les erreurs de flip de bit qui résultent souvent des imperfections matérielles
examples.why: The same concept is rendered two ways in one sentence — « retournements de bits » then the English hybrid « erreurs de flip de bit » — an in-file inconsistency plus an unidiomatic borrowing.

examples.source: the difference between 10 trials (level 1) and 50 trials (level 5) can be dramatic
examples.suggested: … peut être spectaculaire / considérable
examples.translation: la différence entre 10 essais (niveau 1) et 50 essais (niveau 5) peut être dramatique
examples.why: Classic false friend: French « dramatique » carries a tragic connotation, not the English sense of 'very large'.

examples.source: Retrieve the result and map the solution bitstring back to the original graph nodes.
examples.suggested: Récupère le résultat et associe la chaîne de bits solution aux nœuds du graphe d'origine.
examples.translation: Récupère le résultat et mappe le bitstring de solution en retour vers les nœuds du graphe d'origine.
examples.why: « mappe … en retour vers » is a word-for-word calque of 'map back to' that no French technical writer would produce.

examples.source: For support, contact support@kipu-quantum.com.
examples.suggested: Pour obtenir de l'aide, contacte support@kipu-quantum.com.
examples.translation: Pour du soutien, contacte support@kipu-quantum.com.
examples.why: « Pour du soutien » is moral/emotional support in French; the section heading already uses the right register (« Obtenir de l'aide »), so this line is also inconsistent with its own heading.

examples.source: where the Quipu was one of the very first calculation machines developed by mankind 2000 years BCE
examples.suggested: … développées par l'humanité, 2000 ans avant J.-C.
examples.translation: où le Quipu fut l'une des toutes premières machines à calculer développées par l'humanité, il y a 2000 ans avant J.-C.
examples.why: « il y a 2000 ans » (2000 years ago) contradicts « avant J.-C. » in the same phrase; the intended date survives but the wording is self-contradictory.

editor_note: The translation is generally fluent and mathematically faithful, but one sentence inverts a control condition and teaches a false rule. In the Protocol section the English says the classically-controlled X/Z gates "are not applied or applied depending on whether these classical control bits are 0 or 1, respectively"; the French reorders the pair to "les portes sont appliquées ou non selon que ces bits de contrôle classiques valent 0 ou 1, respectivement", which — because "respectivement" binds the order — states that the gate IS applied when the control bit is 0 and NOT applied when it is 1, the exact opposite of the source and of step 3 of the same protocol ("Si $a = 1,$ Bob applique un bit flip"). A learner reading only that sentence would misread every classically-controlled gate in the circuit diagram. Beyond that, the remaining defects are minor: "In words, the teleportation protocol is as follows" becomes "En termes simples" (the English contrasts the prose description with the circuit diagram, not a simplification), "basic quantum information theory" is rendered as the stiff "la théorie quantique de l'information de base", and "such as one involving a third party" loses its exemplifying "such as", turning an example into an exhaustive alternative.

examples.source: It should also be noted that the $X$ and $Z$ gates have *classical* controls, which simply means that the gates are not applied or applied depending on whether these classical control bits are $0$ or $1,$ respectively.
examples.suggested: … ce qui signifie simplement que les portes ne sont pas appliquées, ou sont appliquées, selon que ces bits de contrôle classiques valent $0$ ou $1,$ respectivement.
examples.translation: Il convient également de noter que les portes $X$ et $Z$ ont des contrôles *classiques*, ce qui signifie simplement que les portes sont appliquées ou non selon que ces bits de contrôle classiques valent $0$ ou $1,$ respectivement.
examples.why: The English pairs 'not applied / applied' with '0 / 1'. The French swaps the first pair while keeping 'respectivement', so it asserts the gate is applied on control bit 0 and skipped on 1 — an inverted condition that contradicts step 3 of the same protocol and would make a learner misread the classically-controlled X and Z in the teleportation circuit.

examples.source: In words, the teleportation protocol is as follows:
examples.suggested: En mots, le protocole de téléportation se déroule comme suit :
examples.translation: En termes simples, le protocole de téléportation se déroule comme suit :
examples.why: 'In words' contrasts the prose description with the circuit diagram just shown; 'En termes simples' recasts it as a simplified/informal restatement, changing the pedagogical framing (the list is the full, exact protocol, not a simplified version).

examples.source: This is not too difficult to prove mathematically using basic quantum information theory…
examples.suggested: Ce n'est pas très difficile à démontrer mathématiquement à l'aide des bases de la théorie de l'information quantique…
examples.translation: Ce n'est pas trop difficile à démontrer mathématiquement à l'aide de la théorie quantique de l'information de base…
examples.why: 'la théorie quantique de l'information de base' is a calqued word order in which 'de base' dangles and can be misparsed as 'the basic information'; a French quantum writer would say 'les bases de la théorie de l'information quantique'.

examples.source: Or, it could be that a different process, such as one involving a third party or a complex distributed process, was used to establish this shared e-bit.
examples.suggested: Ou bien, un autre processus — par exemple un processus impliquant une tierce partie ou un processus distribué complexe — a pu être utilisé pour établir cet e-bit partagé.
examples.translation: Ou bien, un autre processus — impliquant une tierce partie ou un processus distribué complexe — a pu être utilisé pour établir cet e-bit partagé.
examples.why: 'such as' marks the two options as illustrations; dropping it makes the appositive read as an exhaustive definition of the alternative process, narrowing a deliberately open statement.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no hallucination, no dropped caveat: the region caveat ("You can access either region by using the same API key, but you can only see and access the instances that were created in the region that you're logged in to"), the trusted-vs-untrusted environment split, and the "these login credentials are not your IBM Cloud account credentials" parenthesis all survive intact, and the informal "tu" register holds everywhere (suis, crée, connecte-toi, assure-toi, essaie). The single thing a native technical editor would change is the zeugma in that same region sentence: "tu ne peux voir et accéder qu'aux instances créées dans la région..." coordinates a direct-object verb (voir) with an indirect-object verb (accéder à) on one complement, which is ungrammatical in careful French; "tu ne peux consulter et utiliser que les instances créées..." fixes it. Terminology is otherwise correct and consistent (QPU, instances, CRN, clé API / token d'API mirroring the source's own key/token alternation, pare-feu, endpoints kept as-is per common French dev usage).

examples.source: you can only see and access the instances that were created in the region that you're logged in to
examples.suggested: tu ne peux consulter et utiliser que les instances créées dans la région à laquelle tu es connecté(e)
examples.translation: tu ne peux voir et accéder qu'aux instances créées dans la région à laquelle tu es connecté(e)
examples.why: Zeugma: 'voir' takes a direct object but 'accéder' requires 'à', so the shared complement 'aux instances' cannot serve both verbs. Meaning is still clear (not misleading), but the coordination is ungrammatical in edited French.

editor_note: Substantively faithful throughout — all the load-bearing technical content is correct and would not mislead: gate counts (10 / 21 / 21n-11 / 9n-5 / 5n-3), the Big-O definitions with their quantifiers ("pour tout n ≥ n_0", "chaque fois que n+m ≥ k_0", "pour *tout* ε > 0"), the deferred-measurement caveat about the classical bit not being overwritten, the O(n²2^(n/2)) trial-division derivation, and the domain terms (bit de retenue, demi-additionneur / additionneur complet, zéros non significatifs, crible algébrique des corps de nombres, exponentiation par carrés répétés, recherche non structurée, uniformité) are all conventional and used consistently. Informal "tu" holds ("considère la figure suivante", "Mais remarque que", "Remarque aussi"). What a native technical editor would change is prose mechanics: one relative clause is genuinely ungrammatical ("des problèmes dont on ne sait pas … d'algorithmes à coût polynomial", ~l.393), "assez moins convaincants" (~l.410) is not a French collocation, "du détail spécifique de si nous considérons" (~l.308) is a raw calque of English "of whether", and "scale better / poor scaling / exponential scaling" is rendered four times by the clunky periphrasis "comportement en termes d'échelle" instead of "passer à l'échelle" / "croissance du coût". One intensifier is dropped: EN "we don't need nearly this many bits" becomes the flatter "il ne faut pas autant de bits" (~l.79). None of these change the meaning taught.

examples.source: The so-called *NP-complete* problems are a class of problems not known to (and widely conjectured not to) have polynomial-cost algorithms.
examples.suggested: Les problèmes dits *NP-complets* forment une classe de problèmes dont on ignore s'ils admettent des algorithmes à coût polynomial — et l'on conjecture largement qu'ils n'en admettent pas.
examples.translation: Les problèmes dits *NP-complets* sont une classe de problèmes dont on ne sait pas (et dont on conjecture largement qu'ils n'ont pas) d'algorithmes à coût polynomial.
examples.why: The relative construction is broken in French: « dont on ne sait pas … d'algorithmes » has no valid antecedent-verb pairing, and the parenthetical cannot share it. A reader parses it twice before recovering the sense.

examples.source: but given the current gap between quantum and classical computing technology, they do seem rather less compelling at the present time.
examples.suggested: …ils paraissent pour l'instant nettement moins convaincants.
examples.translation: mais étant donné l'écart actuel entre les technologies de calcul quantique et classique, ils semblent actuellement assez moins convaincants.
examples.why: « assez moins » is not a French collocation (one says « nettement moins », « bien moins », « un peu moins »), and « actuel » … « actuellement » repeats in the same sentence.

examples.source: Notice also that it doesn't depend on the specific detail of whether we consider XOR gates to have unit cost or cost 7.
examples.suggested: Remarque aussi que cela ne dépend pas du détail que constitue le choix d'attribuer aux portes XOR un coût unitaire ou un coût de 7.
examples.translation: Remarque aussi que cela ne dépend pas du détail spécifique de si nous considérons que les portes XOR ont un coût unitaire ou un coût de $7.$
examples.why: « de si nous considérons » is a direct calque of English "of whether"; French never chains « de » + « si » this way. A native writer nominalizes the choice instead.

examples.source: There are, in fact, other ways to multiply that scale better. / a problem that causes poor scaling / fail to avoid this exponential scaling in cost
examples.suggested: d'autres façons de multiplier qui passent mieux à l'échelle / un problème qui fait mal passer le coût à l'échelle / éviter cette croissance exponentielle du coût
examples.translation: d'autres façons de multiplier qui ont un meilleur comportement en termes d'échelle / cause un mauvais comportement en termes d'échelle / éviter ce comportement exponentiel en termes de coût
examples.why: « comportement en termes d'échelle » is a heavy calque used four times for "scaling"; French complexity writing says « passer à l'échelle », « croissance du coût » or « le coût croît en… ». Meaning survives, but the prose reads as translated rather than written.

examples.source: Note, in particular, that the length (or size) of the input N is not N itself; when N is large we don't need nearly this many bits to express N in binary notation.
examples.suggested: …quand $N$ est grand, il s'en faut de beaucoup qu'on ait besoin d'autant de bits pour exprimer $N$ en notation binaire.
examples.translation: Notons en particulier que la longueur (ou la taille) de l'entrée $N$ n'est pas $N$ lui-même ; quand $N$ est grand, il ne faut pas autant de bits pour exprimer $N$ en notation binaire.
examples.why: "not nearly this many" is an emphatic "far fewer"; « pas autant » only says "not that many". The point of the sentence — the gap between N and lg(N) is enormous — is flattened, though not reversed.

editor_note: No misleading content: the structure, the five SDK bullet points, the ecosystem list and the "Prochaines étapes" admonition all track the English faithfully, and the informal "tu" convention holds throughout ("tu peux exécuter", "consulte la page d'installation", "prêt·e"). What a native technical editor would still change is concentrated in the mthree bullet (l. 58): "solves for corrected measurement probabilities" is calqued as "qui résout des probabilités de mesure corrigées" — one does not "résoudre" probabilities in French (expected: "qui détermine/calcule les probabilités de mesure corrigées") — and the same sentence carries an agreement error, "une méthode itérative préconditionné" instead of "préconditionnée". Two smaller slips: the opening "As quantum technology evolves, so does Qiskit" becomes the stiff causal-reading "Comme la technologie quantique évolue, Qiskit évolue aussi" (idiomatic: "À mesure que… Qiskit évolue également"), and "Benchmarking is important" is upgraded to "Le benchmarking est essentiel", strengthening a claim the source states more moderately. Also "plug into a workflow to scale or design new quantum algorithms" renders "scale" as the vaguer "faire évoluer" rather than "mettre à l'échelle". None of these would make a learner form a false belief.

examples.source: a measurement mitigation technique that solves for corrected measurement probabilities using a dimensionality reduction step followed by either direct LU factorization or a preconditioned iterative method
examples.suggested: une technique d'atténuation des erreurs de mesure qui détermine les probabilités de mesure corrigées à l'aide d'une étape de réduction de dimensionnalité, suivie soit d'une factorisation LU directe, soit d'une méthode itérative préconditionnée
examples.translation: une technique d'atténuation des mesures qui résout des probabilités de mesure corrigées à l'aide d'une étape de réduction de dimensionnalité suivie soit d'une factorisation LU directe, soit d'une méthode itérative préconditionné
examples.why: "résout des probabilités" is a raw calque of "solves for" — the verb résoudre does not take probabilities as an object in French; and "préconditionné" fails to agree with the feminine "méthode".

examples.source: As quantum technology evolves, so does Qiskit, with new capabilities released every year
examples.suggested: À mesure que la technologie quantique évolue, Qiskit évolue également, avec de nouvelles fonctionnalités publiées chaque année
examples.translation: Comme la technologie quantique évolue, Qiskit évolue aussi, avec de nouvelles fonctionnalités publiées chaque année
examples.why: Sentence-initial "Comme" reads as causal ("since") rather than progressive ("as"); the English expresses parallel evolution over time, which "À mesure que" conveys naturally.

examples.source: Benchmarking is important for comparing the relative performance of quantum software
examples.suggested: Le benchmarking est important pour comparer les performances relatives des logiciels quantiques
examples.translation: Le benchmarking est essentiel pour comparer les performances relatives des logiciels quantiques
examples.why: "essentiel" strengthens the source's "important" into a necessity claim the English does not make.

examples.source: Addons are modular software components that plug into a workflow to scale or design new quantum algorithms.
examples.suggested: … qui s'intègrent dans un workflow pour mettre à l'échelle ou concevoir de nouveaux algorithmes quantiques.
examples.translation: Les addons sont des composants logiciels modulaires qui s'intègrent dans un workflow pour faire évoluer ou concevoir de nouveaux algorithmes quantiques.
examples.why: "scale" here is the technical sense (mise à l'échelle, utility-scale); "faire évoluer" flattens it to a generic "make evolve" and loses the connection to "à l'échelle utilitaire" used a sentence earlier.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — I checked the numerically loaded passages (occupancy tables, p(flip)/w(p(flip)) example with h = N/M = 2/4, the "~24 mH vs 1,6 mH de précision chimique" discussion, the alpha/beta column ranges `(N, N/2]` / `(N/2, 0]`, and the two-phase configuration-recovery procedure) and found no inversion, no swapped quantity and no dropped caveat; core terms (chaînes de bits, déterminants de Slater, orbitales de spin, portes de rotation de Givens, opérateur de Coulomb diagonal, transpileur, base computationnelle) are correct and stable. What a native technical editor would still fix: (1) line ~323 leaves the English word untranslated inside a French gloss — "(en abrégé _occupancies_)" where the abbreviation being introduced should be the French "occupations", the term used everywhere else in the file; (2) same sentence breaks the file's informal-"tu" convention with "Notez que" (the file otherwise says "Note que", "ton choix", "ton circuit", "Augmente progressivement"); (3) line ~513 "ce qui manque des vecteurs du support de l'état fondamental" is a syntactic calque of "which is missing vectors" and is ungrammatical in French; (4) "Eigensolver" is rendered two ways — "solveur propre" (~282, ~389) vs "solveur d'états propres" (~361, ~387), and "solveur propre" is the weaker, non-idiomatic of the two; (5) gender-agreement slip at ~149, "les amplitudes `t2` sont ceux des opérateurs" (should be "celles"). None of these would mislead a learner.

examples.source: we can compute probability of electron occupancies (in short _occupancies_) per spin-orbital (qubit)
examples.suggested: nous pouvons calculer la probabilité d'occupation des électrons (en abrégé _occupations_) par orbitale de spin (qubit)
examples.translation: nous pouvons calculer la probabilité d'occupation des électrons (en abrégé _occupancies_) par orbitale de spin (qubit)
examples.why: The gloss introduces a short form the rest of the file then uses in French ("occupation orbitale moyenne", "Occupation (Batch0)"). Leaving the English "occupancies" as the declared French shorthand makes the gloss self-defeating: the abbreviation it announces never reappears.

examples.source: Note that, as per Qiskit ordering convention, the right most bit represents qubit-0 (Q0)
examples.suggested: Note que, selon la convention d'ordre de Qiskit, le bit le plus à droite représente le qubit 0 (Q0)
examples.translation: Notez que, selon la convention d'ordre de Qiskit, le bit le plus à droite représente qubit-0 (Q0)
examples.why: Isolated vouvoiement in an otherwise consistently tutoyed file ("Note que" at 1.2, "ton choix"/"ton gestionnaire"/"ton circuit" in section 2, "Augmente progressivement" in the exercise).

examples.source: the subspace is spanned by max $500$ vectors, which is missing vectors from ground state support
examples.suggested: le sous-espace est engendré par au maximum $500$ vecteurs, auquel il manque donc des vecteurs du support de l'état fondamental
examples.translation: le sous-espace est engendré par au maximum $500$ vecteurs, ce qui manque des vecteurs du support de l'état fondamental
examples.why: "ce qui manque des vecteurs" is a word-for-word transposition of the English relative clause and is not grammatical French; "manquer" cannot take a direct object this way. A French writer would use "auquel il manque…" or "ce qui exclut des vecteurs…".

examples.source: fed into an Eigensolver … Run the eigenstate solver … cycles run by each eigensolver
examples.suggested: use "solveur d'états propres" (or "solveur aux valeurs propres") consistently in all three places
examples.translation: transmis à un solveur propre (Eigensolver) … Exécuter le solveur d'états propres … cycles de Davidson exécutés par chaque solveur propre
examples.why: Two renderings for the same component within one file, and the shorter one, "solveur propre", reads as "clean solver" out of context — the concept stays identifiable but the split is avoidable.

examples.source: `t1` amplitudes are the coefficient of single excitation operators and `t2` amplitudes are for double excitation operators
examples.suggested: … et les amplitudes `t2` sont celles des opérateurs d'excitation double
examples.translation: les amplitudes `t1` sont les coefficients des opérateurs d'excitation simple et les amplitudes `t2` sont ceux des opérateurs d'excitation double
examples.why: "amplitudes" is feminine, so the anaphoric pronoun must be "celles", not "ceux"; a plain agreement slip in otherwise clean prose.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: every claim tracks the English (Open-Plan users can't submit session jobs, "not all of it" → "pas entièrement", the not-open-source / are-open-source contrast keeps its bold polarity), and the informal "tu" register holds throughout ("consulte", "Découvre", "installe-le", "ton ordinateur portable"). What a native technical editor would change is smaller: the product name "Qiskit IBM Provider" is translated *and* reordered into "le fournisseur IBM Qiskit", which reads as a generic vendor rather than the `qiskit-ibm-provider` package; "readout mitigation" becomes "l'atténuation de la lecture" (attenuating the readout itself) where the field says "atténuation des erreurs de lecture"; and "zero-noise extrapolation" is calqued as "extrapolation zéro-bruit" instead of the usual "extrapolation à bruit nul". Two agreement/phrasing slips add friction: "Une fois configurés" agrees with "les utilisateurs" so it reads "once the users are configured" (the English refers to the instance — "Une fois configurée"), and "ressources quantiques-classiques" should be "ressources quantiques et classiques". None of these would make a learner believe something false.

examples.source: is the successor to the Qiskit IBM Provider
examples.suggested: est le successeur de Qiskit IBM Provider (`qiskit-ibm-provider`)
examples.translation: est le successeur du fournisseur IBM Qiskit
examples.why: Product/package name translated and word-order-swapped; "fournisseur" reads as a commercial vendor, so the learner cannot map it onto the `qiskit-ibm-provider` package it names.

editor_note: No semantic drift, hallucination or dropped caveat: every paragraph tracks the English (the "collected now, decrypted later" point, the 6–7 h estimate, the "not intended to be used as actual implementations" admonition, the login prompt on first cell run all survive intact), and the informal "tu" holds throughout with no vous/veuillez slip. The main terminology weakness is "quantum-safe", rendered as the word-order calque "chiffrement quantique sécurisé" (l.30, l.90), which a reader can parse as "quantum encryption" — exactly the confusion this course exists to dispel; the sibling lesson quantum-safe-cryptography.mdx already uses the standard "post-quantique", so this file is also out of step with the course. Remaining issues are naturalness calques rather than meaning: the untranslated English noun in "Un primer de mathématiques" (l.50), "postuler pour un badge" (l.34, which in French means applying for a job), "bibliothèques de sécurité bien supportées et revues" (l.76, anglicism for "prises en charge et auditées"), and the twice-used "tu pourrais souhaiter…" (l.52, l.87) which is a literal transposition of "you may wish to". None of these would teach a learner something false.

examples.source: Quantum-safe encryption schemes / Using quantum-safe encryption in practice
examples.suggested: Les schémas de chiffrement post-quantiques / L'utilisation pratique du chiffrement post-quantique
examples.translation: Les schémas de chiffrement quantique sécurisés / L'utilisation pratique du chiffrement quantique sécurisé
examples.why: "chiffrement quantique sécurisé" is a word-order calque whose default French parse is "secure quantum encryption", i.e. encryption that is itself quantum, rather than classical encryption resistant to quantum attack. Recognizable in context (the preceding bullet contrasts the quantum threat to classical schemes), so MINOR rather than FAIL, but the sibling file quantum-safe-cryptography.mdx already uses "post-quantique" and this file should match.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: the account → users/instances → access-policies hierarchy, the "only one account owner with exclusive billing control" claim, the writer-can-run-jobs-but-not-list-instances caveat, the viewer-on-All-account-management-services billing-visibility warning, and both role tables all match the English exactly, and the informal "tu" register (vuoi, puoi, consulta, clicca) holds throughout. Two things a native technical editor would still change. (1) In the Manager row, "deleting or canceling a job" becomes "l'eliminazione o la cancellazione di un job" — in Italian "cancellazione" reads as a synonym of "eliminazione", so the delete-vs-cancel distinction (two different Qiskit Runtime job operations) collapses into what looks like a redundant pair; "annullamento" is the conventional rendering of "cancel". (2) "clicca il numero" is a transitive calque of "click the number"; Italian takes the preposition ("clicca sul numero" / "fai clic sul numero"). Worth noting for the record, not as a defect: the translation silently corrects the English source's copy-paste error in the second table lead-in ("platform management actions" → "azioni di accesso al servizio"), which now correctly describes the service-access table below it.

examples.source: Permissions beyond the writer role, including provisioning instances, setting the instance cost limit, and deleting or canceling a job
examples.suggested: Permessi oltre al ruolo writer, incluso il provisioning di istanze, l'impostazione del limite di costo dell'istanza e l'eliminazione o l'annullamento di un job
examples.translation: Permessi oltre al ruolo writer, incluso il provisioning di istanze, l'impostazione del limite di costo dell'istanza e l'eliminazione o la cancellazione di un job
examples.why: "cancellazione" in Italian means deletion, so "eliminazione o la cancellazione" reads as the same operation twice and loses the distinction between deleting a job record and cancelling a running job — two separate Qiskit Runtime actions. "annullamento" is the standard rendering of "cancel".

examples.source: Then, for a more detailed list, click the number in the column next to the role name.
examples.suggested: Poi, per un elenco più dettagliato, fai clic sul numero nella colonna accanto al nome del ruolo.
examples.translation: Poi, per un elenco più dettagliato, clicca il numero nella colonna accanto al nome del ruolo.
examples.why: "cliccare" is intransitive in Italian and takes "su"; the direct-object construction is a calque of English "click the number" that a native technical writer would not use.

editor_note: No misleading content: the whole technical spine (linearità come chiusura rispetto a ⊕, controlli di parità ↔ generatori stabilizzatori Z, condizione CSS D_Z⊆C_X, i due casi della proiezione Π) is faithful, the tu-register holds ("Nota in particolare", "considera i restanti tre generatori"), and core terms (parole di codice, prodotto scalare binario, spazio codice, codici duali) are correct. What a native editor would still change is a set of within-file splits that fall almost exactly at the halfway point of the file, as if two passes were merged: "generatori $Z$ stabilizzatori" (a calque of the English word order, lines 164–274) becomes "generatori stabilizzatori $Z$" from line 278 on; "codice di Hamming $[7,4,3]$" (lines 46–181) becomes the calqued "codice $[7,4,3]$-Hamming" (lines 294–423); "base standard" is used throughout but line 181 says "base computazionale"; and "errore di inversione di bit" (line 66) later becomes the untranslated "bit flip" (lines 278, 294). One dropped qualifier is worth fixing on its own: at line 300 "up to the *minimum* of $j$ and $k$" is rendered "pari al *minimo* tra $j$ e $k$" (equal to, not up to), even though the same paragraph correctly renders the two earlier "up to" as "fino a $j$/$k$ errori". Also line 71 renders "more efficient ways" as "modi migliori ed efficaci" (effective, not efficient) and line 357 uses the nonstandard "contenenza" where Italian mathematical usage is "inclusione".

examples.source: It then follows, by the discretization of errors, that this CSS code can correct for *any error* on a number of qubits up to the *minimum* of $j$ and $k.$
examples.suggested: ... su un numero di qubit fino al *minimo* tra $j$ e $k$.
examples.translation: Ne consegue, per la discretizzazione degli errori, che questo codice CSS può correggere *qualsiasi errore* su un numero di qubit pari al *minimo* tra $j$ e $k$.
examples.why: "up to the minimum" becomes "pari al minimo" (exactly equal to), dropping the bound qualifier. The same paragraph translates the two preceding "up to" correctly as "fino a $j$ errori"/"fino a $k$ errori", so the inconsistency is internal to one paragraph.

examples.source: Let us give the name *$Z$ stabilizer generators* ... / the $Z$ stabilizer generators describe a code that protects against bit flips
examples.suggested: Use "generatori stabilizzatori $Z$" (and "$X$") throughout, including in the naming sentence at line 164 and the definition at line 196.
examples.translation: Chiamiamo *generatori $Z$ stabilizzatori* ... / i generatori stabilizzatori $Z$ descrivono un codice che protegge dai bit flip
examples.why: The file names the concept with the calqued English order "generatori $Z$ stabilizzatori" (lines 164, 168, 196, 199, 201, 213, 239, 270, 273) and then silently switches to the natural Italian "generatori stabilizzatori $Z$" from line 278 onward. Both are recognizable, but the coined term should match the term used later.

examples.source: the $[7,4,3]$-Hamming code
examples.suggested: codice di Hamming $[7,4,3]$ everywhere
examples.why: Same split at the halfway point. "codice $[7,4,3]$-Hamming" is an English-word-order calque; Italian puts the eponym after the noun with "di".

examples.source: which we get by applying Hadamard operations to the standard basis states that correspond to the strings in the $[7,4,3]$-Hamming code
examples.suggested: ... agli stati della base standard corrispondenti ...
examples.translation: che si ottengono applicando operazioni di Hadamard agli stati della base computazionale corrispondenti alle stringhe nel codice di Hamming $[7,4,3]$
examples.why: "standard basis" is rendered "base standard" everywhere else in the file (lines 167, 331, 372, 403) and the contrast with the $\{|+\rangle,|-\rangle\}$ basis is built on that name; the one-off "base computazionale" breaks the pairing.

examples.source: There are better, more efficient ways to describe classical linear codes, including the following two ways.
examples.suggested: Esistono modi migliori e più efficienti per descrivere i codici lineari classici, tra cui i due seguenti.
examples.translation: Esistono modi migliori ed efficaci per descrivere i codici lineari classici, tra cui i seguenti due.
examples.why: "efficaci" means effective, not efficient, and the comparative "more" is lost, so the contrast with simply listing all codewords (the point of the sentence) is flattened.

examples.source: Alternatively, by reversing the roles of the $X$ and $Z$ stabilizer generators and starting from the containment $\mathcal{D}_X\subseteq\mathcal{C}_Z,$ we can reach the same conclusion.
examples.suggested: ... e partendo dall'inclusione $\mathcal{D}_X\subseteq\mathcal{C}_Z,$ ...
examples.translation: In alternativa, scambiando i ruoli dei generatori stabilizzatori $X$ e $Z$ e partendo dalla contenenza $\mathcal{D}_X\subseteq\mathcal{C}_Z,$ si giunge alla stessa conclusione.
examples.why: "contenenza" is not the term Italian mathematical writing uses for set containment; "inclusione" is standard and matches the $\subseteq$ relation named earlier in the same section.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the version-stability caveat (v2.4.0 build works with v2.4.1 but may break on v2.5.0), the `static` linkage rationale, the `PyInit__core` double-underscore rule and the borrow-semantics warning all match the English with no drift, and the informal "tu" register is consistent (Puoi/Devi/Dovresti/Parti/Consulta). What an editor would change: "C API" is rendered two ways within the file — Italianized "L'API C di Qiskit" (lines 12, 29, 34) versus the English-order "la C API di Qiskit" (lines 120, 219, 238, 241, 423, 472, 474), the two even colliding in one sentence at line 29 ("L'API C di Qiskit è esposta … in modo molto simile alla C API di NumPy"); pick one and unify. Two calques stiffen the prose: "è garantito per funzionare" (line 37) and "che è puramente in termini di tipi Python" (line 368); "la vera estensione C" (line 213) should be "l'estensione C vera e propria". At line 427 the pronoun "le" in "l'oggetto Python che le supporta mentre le usi" grammatically attaches to "funzioni" instead of the borrowed C-native objects, and the English "while using the result" is collapsed — the caveat still lands, but the reference is muddied.

examples.source: The Qiskit C API can be used within Python extension modules. … The Qiskit C API is exposed for Python extension modules in a very similar manner to the NumPy C API.
examples.suggested: Use "l'API C" everywhere (…in modo molto simile all'API C di NumPy), including lines 120, 219, 238, 241, 423, 472, 474.
examples.translation: L'API C di Qiskit può essere usata all'interno di moduli di estensione Python. … L'API C di Qiskit è esposta per i moduli di estensione Python in modo molto simile alla C API di NumPy.
examples.why: The same term alternates between Italian word order ("API C") and the English-order calque ("C API") within the file, and both appear in a single sentence. The concept stays identifiable, so this is MINOR, but a native editor would unify it.

examples.source: an extension module using Qiskit v2.4.0 at build time is guaranteed to work with Qiskit v2.4.1 at runtime
examples.suggested: …ne è garantito il funzionamento con Qiskit v2.4.1 a runtime / funzionerà con certezza con Qiskit v2.4.1 a runtime
examples.translation: un modulo di estensione che usa Qiskit v2.4.0 al momento della compilazione è garantito per funzionare con Qiskit v2.4.1 a runtime
examples.why: "è garantito per funzionare" is a direct calque of "is guaranteed to work"; Italian does not use "garantito per + infinito" this way. Grammatical and unambiguous, so MINOR.

examples.source: you should take care not to release your reference to the Python object that backs them, while using the result
examples.suggested: devi fare attenzione a non rilasciare il riferimento all'oggetto Python che li contiene finché stai usando il risultato
examples.translation: devi fare attenzione a non rilasciare il riferimento all'oggetto Python che le supporta mentre le usi
examples.why: The feminine plural "le" points back to "funzioni" rather than to the borrowed C-native objects, and "while using the result" is flattened into "mentre le usi". The caveat is still conveyed, so this is a clarity slip, not drift.

editor_note: Faithful and natively written throughout, with correct and consistent domain renderings (prodotto tensoriale, vettore di stato alongside the kept `Statevector`, "il qubit a sinistra è il controllo e il qubit a destra è il bersaglio", "Per impostazione predefinita, `measure` misura tutti i qubit"), the spin left/right caveat ("non si riferiscono al qubit più a destra o più a sinistra") and the Qiskit right-to-left numbering note preserved exactly; the only cosmetic nit is a stray space in `"+" ,` in the spin paragraph, which is below defect threshold.

Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no hallucination, no dropped caveat: the `local_mode` polarity (False → remoto tramite il Qiskit Transpiler Service / True → locale con fallback al cloud) is correct, block sizes (nove / 65, 33 e 27 / sei qubit) match, and the `replace_only_if_better=False` and "emetteranno un avviso e lasceranno il sotto-circuito originale invariato" caveats are intact. Terminology is consistent and conventional (transpilazione, i pass, coupling map, sottografo connesso, gate, sintesi/ri-sintetizzare) and the informal "tu" holds (installa, Visita, Puoi, Consulta). Two spots read stiffly and a native technical editor would reorder them: "forzare la sostituzione sempre impostando…" (adverb misplaced — "forzare sempre la sostituzione") and "al numero desiderato di thread massimi" (hyperbaton — "al numero massimo di thread desiderato"). Neither misleads; they are pure fluency polish.

examples.source: but this can be forced to always replace the circuit by setting `replace_only_if_better=False`.
examples.suggested: ma è possibile forzare sempre la sostituzione impostando `replace_only_if_better=False`.
examples.translation: ma è possibile forzare la sostituzione sempre impostando `replace_only_if_better=False`.
examples.why: Calqued English adverb position; in Italian 'sempre' belongs before the noun phrase it modifies, and trailing 'sempre' reads as machine-ordered rather than written.

examples.source: You can also set the environment variable `AI_TRANSPILER_MAX_THREADS` to the desired number of maximum threads
examples.suggested: Puoi anche impostare la variabile d'ambiente `AI_TRANSPILER_MAX_THREADS` al numero massimo di thread desiderato
examples.translation: Puoi anche impostare la variabile d'ambiente `AI_TRANSPILER_MAX_THREADS` al numero desiderato di thread massimi
examples.why: 'thread massimi' splits the adjective from the head it qualifies ('numero massimo'); the current order is grammatical but stiff and no Italian technical writer would phrase it this way.

editor_note: Semantically faithful throughout — every quantity, case split and probability claim matches the English (2^{n-1} elementi in range(f), probabilità superiore al 99,9%, almeno 1 - 2^{-r}, fallirà ... con probabilità almeno 1/2), core terms are right and consistent (one-to-one → "funzione iniettiva", two-to-one → "due-a-uno", preimage → "preimmagine", null space → "*nucleo* (null space)" glossed on first use then consistent). What a native technical editor would still change: (a) "entries" of a matrix/vector is rendered three-quarters of the way as "voci" (righe 259, 278) but as "elementi a valori binari" at riga 237 — "voci" is the wrong register for matrix entries (it means list/dictionary entries) and the split is internal inconsistency; (b) "vantaggio del quantum rispetto agli algoritmi classici" (righe 15, 304) is a raw anglicism where Italian wants "vantaggio quantistico" / "degli algoritmi quantistici rispetto a quelli classici"; (c) "buckets" → "secchi" (riga 143) is a pail-literalism no Italian author would use for bucketing a sum; (d) riga 290 is ungrammatical — "Quante query ha bisogno un algoritmo…" is missing the required "Di" ("Di quante query ha bisogno…"); (e) "lo XOR esclusivo" (riga 300) is pleonastic (XOR already is exclusive-OR). None of these mislead a learner.

examples.source: we perform the multiplication as usual and then take the remainder of the entries of the result after dividing by 2 … the vector whose entries are the bits of s
examples.suggested: …il resto degli elementi del risultato… / …il vettore i cui elementi sono i bit di s
examples.translation: eseguiamo la moltiplicazione normalmente e poi prendiamo il resto delle voci del risultato dopo la divisione per 2 … il vettore le cui voci sono i bit di s
examples.why: "voci" means entries in the sense of list/dictionary items; the Italian linear-algebra term for matrix/vector entries is "elementi" (or "componenti"). The file already uses "elementi a valori binari" at riga 237 for the same English word, so the rendering is also inconsistent within the file.

examples.source: an *exponential* advantage of quantum over classical (including probabilistic) algorithms … a striking advantage of quantum over classical algorithms
examples.suggested: un vantaggio *esponenziale* degli algoritmi quantistici su quelli classici … un notevole vantaggio quantistico rispetto agli algoritmi classici
examples.translation: un vantaggio *esponenziale* del quantum rispetto agli algoritmi classici … un notevole vantaggio del quantum rispetto agli algoritmi classici
examples.why: "del quantum" is an untranslated English nominal used as a noun; Italian technical prose says "vantaggio quantistico" or names the algorithms. Reads as machine output rather than as an Italian physicist writing.

examples.source: we're basically just putting these strings into separate buckets depending on which output string z = f(x) they produce … and then summing separately over all the buckets
examples.suggested: …raggruppando queste stringhe in contenitori distinti … e poi sommando separatamente su ogni gruppo
examples.translation: stiamo fondamentalmente mettendo queste stringhe in secchi separati a seconda della stringa di output z = f(x) che producono … e poi sommando separatamente su tutti i secchi
examples.why: "secchio" is a physical pail; the bucketing metaphor for partitioning a sum is normally "gruppi"/"contenitori" (or the loanword "bucket") in Italian technical writing. The pedagogical image survives but the wording is a literalism.

examples.source: How many queries does a *classical* query algorithm need to solve Simon's problem?
examples.suggested: Di quante query ha bisogno un algoritmo di query *classico* per risolvere il problema di Simon?
examples.translation: Quante query ha bisogno un algoritmo di query *classico* per risolvere il problema di Simon?
examples.why: "avere bisogno" governs "di"; without it the section-opening question is ungrammatical — an English word-order carry-over that a native editor would fix immediately.

editor_note: No semantic drift: every claim in the QPU-versioning rules, the SPAM/prob_meas definitions, the 2Q/EPLG/layer-fidelity passages and the `error = 1` caveat matches the English, and informal "tu" holds throughout (Puoi, assicurati, fai clic, dovresti procedere con cautela). What a native technical editor would change is (a) a grammar slip in the EPLG paragraph — "il minimo errore trovato in **una** sottoinsieme di catena di lunghezza `N`" (wrong gender + garbled noun chain for "a subset length N chain"); (b) English "layer/layered" is rendered three ways in the same file — "strati alternati di Clifford" (Median 2Q), "stratificato"/"catena stratificata" (2Q layered), and untranslated "fedeltà del layer" / "quanti layer di un circuito 100x100" (CLOPS); (c) calqued syntax in the versioning section, "il circuito **è garantito per funzionare**" / "non è garantito per funzionare" and "Il numero di versione della revisione **si incrementerà**", where Italian wants "ne è garantita l'esecuzione" / "verrà incrementato". Also "pura **defasatura**" for pure dephasing (standard term is "defasamento") and the bare table cell "Modifiche campione" for "Sample changes", which reads as "example changes" rather than changes to the physical sample. None of these would mislead a learner.

examples.source: the value reported for number of qubits `N` is the lowest error found in a subset length `N` chain searching over the six 100-qubit chains
examples.suggested: il valore riportato per un numero di qubit `N` è l'errore più basso trovato in una sottocatena di lunghezza `N`, cercando fra le sei catene da 100 qubit
examples.translation: il valore riportato per il numero di qubit `N` è il minimo errore trovato in una sottoinsieme di catena di lunghezza `N` ricercando nelle sei catene da 100 qubit
examples.why: Grammatically broken ('una sottoinsieme', masculine noun with feminine article) and the noun chain 'sottoinsieme di catena' obscures the idea of a length-N sub-chain. Meaning is still recoverable, so MINOR, not FAIL.

examples.source: alternating layers of single-qubit Cliffords / layered chain / layer fidelity (LF) / Circuit layer operations per second
examples.suggested: pick one convention — e.g. keep 'layer' throughout ('strati alternati' → 'layer alternati', 'catena stratificata' → 'catena a layer') so LF/EPLG/CLOPS all read consistently
examples.translation: strati alternati di Clifford … catena stratificata … fedeltà del layer (LF) … Le operazioni di layer di circuito al secondo
examples.why: The same English concept 'layer' appears as strati, stratificato and layer within the same file; the concept stays identifiable, so this is within-file inconsistency (MINOR) rather than a false concept.

examples.source: A circuit compiled for a given version number is guaranteed to run on that QPU. … the circuit is not guaranteed to run, although it may do so. The revision version number will increment for fixes that…
examples.suggested: Per un circuito compilato per un dato numero di versione è garantita l'esecuzione su quella QPU. … l'esecuzione del circuito non è garantita, anche se potrebbe comunque funzionare. Il numero di revisione verrà incrementato in caso di correzioni che…
examples.translation: Un circuito compilato per un dato numero di versione è garantito per funzionare su quella QPU. … il circuito non è garantito per funzionare, sebbene possa farlo. Il numero di versione della revisione si incrementerà per correzioni che…
examples.why: 'è garantito per funzionare' and reflexive 'si incrementerà' are direct calques of the English passive/'will increment'; grammatical but no Italian technical writer would phrase it this way.

examples.source: the probability of measuring a qubit in the 0 state when it was intended to be prepared in the |1⟩ state
examples.suggested: la probabilità di misurare un qubit nello stato 0 quando avrebbe dovuto essere preparato nello stato $|1\rangle$
examples.translation: la probabilità di misurare un qubit nello stato 0 quando era previsto di essere preparato nello stato $|1\rangle$
examples.why: 'era previsto di essere preparato' is a literal rendering of 'was intended to be prepared' that Italian does not build this way; the intended-vs-measured contrast, which is the whole pedagogical point of prob_meas0_prep1, lands less crisply.

examples.source: Sample changes (Major version column) / pure dephasing processes
examples.suggested: Modifiche al campione (sostituzione del chip) / processi di puro defasamento
examples.translation: Modifiche campione / processi di pura defasatura
examples.why: 'Modifiche campione' reads as 'sample/example modifications' rather than changes to the physical qubit sample; 'defasatura' is a non-standard variant where the field uses 'defasamento'. Both are recognizable, hence MINOR.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout and nothing would mislead a learner: the collapse/projection argument, the product-state conclusion ("La cosa fondamentale è che si tratta di uno stato prodotto"), the "single-qubit operation can't change the logical qubit" caveat, and the Kraus/generalization sections all track the English exactly, with consistent terminology (sindrome, matrici di Pauli, stato prodotto, matrice densità, prodotti tensoriali) and a natural first-person-plural teaching register. Two small qualifier/reference losses in the opening of the unitary section: "a very small rotation of the Bloch sphere" becomes just "una piccola rotazione della sfera di Bloch" (the intensifier that sets up the later "errori minuscoli e quasi impercettibili" is gone), and "there are infinitely many possible errors like this" is compressed to "le possibilità sono infinite", dropping the anchor to *this kind* of error. Neither changes the physics; both are the sort of thing a native technical editor would restore.

examples.source: such an error could correspond to a very small rotation of the Bloch sphere, possibly representing an error incurred by a gate that isn't perfect
examples.suggested: un tale errore potrebbe corrispondere a una rotazione molto piccola della sfera di Bloch, che rappresenta magari l'errore introdotto da un gate non perfetto
examples.translation: un tale errore potrebbe corrispondere a una piccola rotazione della sfera di Bloch, che rappresenta magari l'errore introdotto da un gate non perfetto
examples.why: The intensifier "very" is dropped. It is load-bearing pedagogically: it sets up the later paragraph about "errori minuscoli e quasi impercettibili di per sé" and the contrast with the next sentence's "non necessariamente vicina all'identità". Not misleading, but a weakened qualifier.

examples.source: After all, there are infinitely many possible errors like this, and it's inconceivable that we could somehow identify each error exactly and then undo it.
examples.suggested: Dopotutto, gli errori possibili di questo tipo sono infiniti, ed è inconcepibile riuscire a identificare esattamente ciascuno di essi per poi annullarlo.
examples.translation: Dopotutto, le possibilità sono infinite, ed è inconcepibile riuscire a identificare ogni errore esattamente e poi annullarlo.
examples.why: "le possibilità sono infinite" loses the explicit referent ("errors like this") and reads as a vaguer, more idiomatic-but-emptier phrase than the source; also "identificare ogni errore esattamente" keeps English adverb placement where Italian would put "esattamente" before the object.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no dropped caveats, no hallucination; the DAG node-colour list, the `apply_operation_back`/`front` semantics, the TransformationPass-vs-AnalysisPass contrast and the layer-by-layer swap-insertion explanation all match the English exactly, and terminology is correct and consistent ("archi diretti", "nodi di operazione", "coupling map" kept in English, "transpilazione"/"transpilare", "pass" invariant, "strato per strato", informal "tu" in "Usa la funzione…", "consulta la guida"). Two things a native technical editor would still change: in the "Aggiungere un'operazione in testa" section the clitic in "rendendola di fatto la prima operazione eseguita" does not agree with its antecedent "il gate specificato" (should be "rendendolo"); and "portare i qubit coinvolti in adiacenza" is a literal calque of "bring … into adjacency" that Italian would express as "rendere adiacenti i qubit coinvolti". Neither can mislead a learner — both are surface polish.

examples.source: This inserts the specified gate before all existing operations in the circuit, effectively making it the first operation executed.
examples.suggested: Questo inserisce il gate specificato prima di tutte le operazioni già presenti nel circuito, rendendolo di fatto la prima operazione eseguita.
examples.translation: Questo inserisce il gate specificato prima di tutte le operazioni già presenti nel circuito, rendendola di fatto la prima operazione eseguita.
examples.why: The English "it" refers to the gate; in Italian the clitic -la does not agree with the masculine "il gate specificato" that governs the gerund clause, so the sentence reads as a grammatical slip. Meaning is still recoverable, hence minor.

examples.source: a suitable swap path is identified, and the required swaps are inserted to bring the involved qubits into adjacency.
examples.suggested: …gli swap necessari vengono inseriti per rendere adiacenti i qubit coinvolti.
examples.translation: viene identificato un percorso di swap adeguato e gli swap necessari vengono inseriti per portare i qubit coinvolti in adiacenza.
examples.why: "portare … in adiacenza" is a word-for-word calque of "bring into adjacency"; an Italian technical writer would use the adjectival construction "rendere adiacenti". Purely stylistic — the instruction is still clear.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: the theorem statement, the C p^2 bound, the p_th = 1/C condition, the (Cp)^{2^k-1} p chain and the 0.1%-1% surface-code figure are all faithful, and the informal "tu" register holds throughout ("immaginiamo", "Prenditi un momento"). What a native technical editor would change is lexical: "una scelta impratica" uses a non-standard adjective (Italian has "impraticabile" / "poco pratica"); the contrast to "doppiamente esponenziale" is rendered as "aumenta solo *singolarmente in modo esponenziale*", which parses more naturally as "individually, exponentially" than as "singly exponential"; "cresce di al più un fattore" has inverted word order (should be "cresce al più di un fattore"); "dell'ordine dallo 0,1% all'1%" is ungrammatical as a partitive ("dell'ordine dello 0,1%-1%"); and the closing "ci fornisce ottimismo mentre continuiamo a spingere avanti" is a double calque of "provide us with optimism / push forward". Also the source hedge "a somewhat informal statement" loses "somewhat", and "probably unlikely to be achievable in practice" is softened to "probabilmente difficile da raggiungere" — neither misleads a learner, but both shade the claim.

examples.source: This would be an impractical choice for an actual physical implementation
examples.suggested: Questa sarebbe una scelta poco pratica (o impraticabile) per un'implementazione fisica reale
examples.translation: Questa sarebbe una scelta impratica per un'implementazione fisica reale
examples.why: 'impratica' is not standard Italian; the usual adjectives are 'poco pratica' or 'impraticabile'. Meaning is still recoverable, so MINOR.

examples.source: the size only increases *singly exponentially* in the number of levels $k.$ ... the size grows by at most a factor determined by the maximum size of the gadgets
examples.suggested: la dimensione cresce solo *in modo semplicemente esponenziale* nel numero di livelli $k.$ ... la dimensione cresce al più di un fattore determinato dalla dimensione massima dei gadget
examples.translation: la dimensione aumenta solo *singolarmente in modo esponenziale* nel numero di livelli $k.$ ... la dimensione cresce di al più un fattore determinato dalla dimensione massima dei gadget
examples.why: 'singolarmente' reads as 'individually/oddly' rather than carrying the singly-vs-doubly exponential contrast, and 'cresce di al più un fattore' puts the quantifier in the wrong slot. Stiff, not misleading.

examples.source: provide us with optimism as we continue to push forward to reach the ultimate goal
examples.suggested: ci danno motivo di ottimismo mentre continuiamo ad andare avanti verso l'obiettivo finale
examples.translation: ci fornisce ottimismo mentre continuiamo a spingere avanti per raggiungere l'obiettivo finale
examples.why: 'fornire ottimismo' and 'spingere avanti' are word-for-word calques of the English; a native technical writer would use 'dare motivo di ottimismo' and 'andare avanti / procedere'.

examples.source: the threshold has been estimated to be on the order of 0.1% to 1%
examples.suggested: si stima che la soglia sia dell'ordine dello 0,1%-1%
examples.translation: la soglia è stata stimata essere dell'ordine dallo 0,1% all'1%
examples.why: 'dell'ordine dallo ... all' ...' is not a well-formed Italian partitive construction; the whole sentence also reads as a calque of the English passive 'has been estimated to be'.

examples.source: Here is a somewhat informal statement of this theorem. / it is minuscule and probably unlikely to be achievable in practice
examples.suggested: una formulazione in qualche modo informale / e probabilmente non raggiungibile nella pratica
examples.translation: Di seguito ne viene riportata una formulazione informale. / è minuscolo e probabilmente difficile da raggiungere in pratica
examples.why: Two hedges are shaded: 'somewhat' is dropped, and 'unlikely to be achievable' is weakened to merely 'difficult to achieve'. Neither changes the conclusion a learner draws, so MINOR rather than FAIL.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: every quantitative claim survives intact (QPU時間は回路容量に依存しますが、それ以外は量子ビット数に依存しません; 最大2倍の回路容量; the accuracy formula and all six benchmark table rows), and core terminology is correct and consistent throughout (mitigation→緩和, suppression→抑制, characterization→特性評価, observable→オブザーバブル, expectation value→期待値, transpilation→トランスパイレーション, unbiased→不偏). The defects are editorial. (1) "Transverse-Field Ising model" is rendered 横断磁場Isingモデル — a literal calque; the established Japanese term is 横磁場イジング模型/横磁場Isingモデル. (2) The "correspondingly" that maps the two (θ_zz, θ_x) parameter pairs to the 40-qubit and 119-qubit rows is dropped (no それぞれ), losing the pairing cue. (3) The two "Review [paper]" bullets in Next steps become the bare noun "レビュー [Bauman…]。" — ungrammatical as an instruction, and inconsistent with the sibling bullet in the same list which correctly uses ～をご覧ください. (4) The Get support section carries a dense layer of keigo (ご連絡いただくこともできます, ご提供ください, 最善のご体験をお届けするため) beyond the file's desu/masu convention. (5) "saved your account to your local environment" drops ローカル環境に.

examples.source: Trotterized Hamiltonian simulation circuits are for a Transverse-Field Ising model at fractional angles
examples.suggested: …分数角度での横磁場Isingモデル用のものです
examples.translation: トロッタライズドハミルトニアンシミュレーション回路は、分数角度での横断磁場Isingモデル用のものです
examples.why: 横断磁場 is a word-by-word calque of "transverse field". Japanese condensed-matter/quantum literature uniformly writes 横磁場イジング模型 (or 横磁場Isingモデル). Recognizable, so not misleading, but a native technical writer would not write 横断磁場.

examples.source: $(\theta_{zz}, \theta_x) = (\pi / 4, \pi /8)$ and $(\theta_{zz}, \theta_x) = (\pi / 6, \pi / 8)$ correspondingly
examples.suggested: …および$(\theta_{zz}, \theta_x) = (\pi / 6, \pi / 8)$（それぞれ40量子ビット回路と119量子ビット回路に対応）
examples.translation: $(\theta_{zz}, \theta_x) = (\pi / 4, \pi /8)$および$(\theta_{zz}, \theta_x) = (\pi / 6, \pi / 8)$
examples.why: "correspondingly" is dropped, so the reader loses the cue that the two angle pairs map in order onto the 40-qubit and 119-qubit table rows. A dropped qualifier, not an inversion — the numbers themselves are unchanged.

examples.source: - Review [Bauman, N. P., et al. (2025). Coupled Cluster Downfolding Theory…]
examples.suggested: - [Bauman, N. P., et al. (2025). Coupled Cluster Downfolding Theory…]を確認してください。
examples.translation: - レビュー [Bauman, N. P., et al. (2025). Coupled Cluster Downfolding Theory…]。
examples.why: The English imperative "Review X" is rendered as the bare noun レビュー followed by a link, which is not a Japanese sentence and reads as an untranslated stub. The preceding bullet in the same list handles the same pattern correctly with ～をご覧ください, so the list is internally inconsistent too.

examples.source: You can also contact your dedicated Qedma POC representative via email or phone. / We are committed to providing you with prompt and effective support to ensure you have the best possible experience with our Qiskit Function.
examples.suggested: また、メールまたは電話で担当のQedma POC担当者に連絡することもできます。／…最善の体験を提供できるよう、迅速で効果的なサポートの提供に努めています。
examples.translation: また、メールまたは電話で担当のQedma POC担当者にご連絡いただくこともできます。／…Qiskit Functionでの最善のご体験をお届けするため、迅速かつ効果的なサポートの提供にコミットしています。
examples.why: ご連絡いただく / ご体験 / お届けする pile keigo onto a doc whose convention is plain desu/masu. The English is polite but not honorific. Also コミットしています is a katakana calque where 努めています reads naturally.

editor_note: The mathematics is faithful throughout — definitions, the rank(ρ) necessary-and-sufficient claim, the Schmidt-decomposition derivation, the bit-commitment argument and the HJW proof all match the English, and register is consistent desu/masu with no keigo. The one substantive defect is a two-pass split in the file's central term: "purification" is 純粋化 through the first two thirds (title, headings 純粋化の定義 / 純粋化の存在 / 純粋化のユニタリ同値性) but becomes 浄化 from the superdense-coding section onward (浄化のユニタリ等価性, 完全混合状態の浄化, 2つの異なる浄化), and "unitary equivalence" splits in parallel between ユニタリ同値性 (heading, theorem box) and ユニタリ等価性 (all later body text) — so the named theorem the last 30% keeps invoking has a different name from the section that proves it. Secondary: line ~402 softens "does immediately imply that superdense coding is possible" to 示唆されます ("is suggested"), which weakens a logical entailment into a hint, and the safe-analogy sentence at line ~417 is a broken run-on where なぜなら…ので never closes before the contrasting concealing clause. 純粋化 is the standard rendering and should win throughout.

examples.source: By the unitary equivalence of purifications, we immediately conclude that ...
examples.suggested: 純粋化のユニタリ同値性から、…が直ちに結論づけられます
examples.translation: 浄化のユニタリ等価性から、…が直ちに結論づけられます
examples.why: From the superdense-coding section onward every occurrence of "purification" switches from 純粋化 (used in the title, all three headings and the definition/theorem boxes) to 浄化, a word that in ordinary Japanese means spiritual/physical cleansing and is not the standard quantum-information term. Same split for "unitary equivalence": ユニタリ同値性 in the heading and theorem box vs ユニタリ等価性 in all later prose.

examples.source: the unitary equivalence of purifications does immediately imply that superdense coding is possible.
examples.suggested: 純粋化のユニタリ同値性から、超高密度符号化が可能であることが直ちに導かれます。
examples.translation: 浄化のユニタリ等価性によって超高密度符号化が可能であることがすぐに示唆されます。
examples.why: The English emphatic "does immediately imply" is a logical entailment; 示唆されます renders it as a mere suggestion/hint, softening a proof-level consequence into speculation right after the sentence conceding that the details are not revealed.

examples.source: Alice has committed to the binary value written on the paper because the safe is in Bob's possession (so it's binding), but because Bob can't open the safe he can't tell which value Alice committed to (so it's concealing).
examples.suggested: アリスは紙に書いた二値にコミットしたことになります。金庫がボブの手元にあるため、アリスは考えを変えられません（拘束力）。一方、ボブは金庫を開けられないので、アリスがどの値にコミットしたかわかりません（秘匿性）。
examples.translation: アリスは紙に書いた二値にコミットしています。なぜなら、金庫はボブの手元にあるので（拘束力）、ボブは金庫を開けられないためアリスがどの値にコミットしたかわかりません（秘匿性）。
examples.why: The なぜなら clause opens a reason but never closes before the sentence slides into the second, contrasting clause; the English "but" contrast between binding and concealing is lost and the result reads as a run-on that a native technical writer would split into two sentences.

examples.source: which describes a pure state of the pair (X,Y), is therefore a purification of ρ.
examples.suggested: は対 $(\mathsf{X},\mathsf{Y})$ の純粋状態を記述するもので、したがって $\rho$ の純粋化となります。
examples.translation: は対 $(\mathsf{X},\mathsf{Y})$ の純粋状態を記述するため、$\rho$ の純粋化となります。
examples.why: The English "therefore" points back at the spectral decomposition just constructed; the Japanese ため turns "describes a pure state of the pair" into the reason it is a purification, which on its own would be a false criterion (being a pure state of the pair is necessary, not sufficient).

examples.source: implications of this theorem / has implications concerning / The last implication of the unitary equivalence of purifications
examples.suggested: 含意 を一貫して使用（…の最後の含意）
examples.translation: 含意 / 示唆を与えます / 最後の応用
examples.why: "Implication" is rendered three ways within the file — 含意, 示唆, 応用 — and 応用 ("application") in particular reframes a logical consequence of the theorem as a practical use of it.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful end-to-end — the approximation-degree direction (0.0 が最大近似、1.0 が近似なし), the "fewer CX at the cost of synthesis fidelity" trade-off, the virtual→physical initial_layout mapping, and the asap/alap gloss (可能な限り qubit を基底状態に保ちます) all match the English, with no inverted conditions or invented claims. Two things a native technical editor would fix: in the approximation-degree paragraph the sentence 「…ゲート数も少なくなります（…ため）、実行しやすくなります。」 breaks grammatically — a polite ます-form is followed by 「、」 and a continuing clause instead of the 連用形 (少なくなり) — and the same sentence drops the English hedge "likely", turning "will also likely have fewer gates" into a flat assertion. In the FakeSherbrooke note, 「Qiskit 互換の実際のまたは偽の Backend」 is a calque of "real or fake backend"; 実機またはフェイクの… would be idiomatic. Register is consistent desu/masu with no keigo.

examples.source: ...but will also likely have fewer gates (because any arbitrary two-qubit operation can be decomposed perfectly with at most three CX gates) and is easier to run.
examples.suggested: ゲート数は少なくなる可能性が高く（任意の 2 量子ビット演算は最大 3 つの CX ゲートで完全に分解できるため）、実行も容易になります。
examples.translation: ゲート数も少なくなります（任意の 2 量子ビット演算は最大 3 つの CX ゲートで完全に分解できるため）、実行しやすくなります。
examples.why: A polite ます-form (少なくなります) is followed by 「、」 and a further clause, which is ungrammatical in Japanese; the 連用形 is required to conjoin. Reads as unedited MT at the seam.

examples.source: but will also likely have fewer gates
examples.suggested: ゲート数は少なくなる可能性が高く
examples.translation: ゲート数も少なくなります
examples.why: The English hedge "likely" is dropped, strengthening a probabilistic tendency into a guarantee. Not misleading enough to teach a false concept, but the qualifier should be restored.

examples.source: but you can try it on any Qiskit-compatible real or fake backend.
examples.suggested: Qiskit 互換であれば、実機でもフェイク Backend でも試すことができます。
examples.translation: Qiskit 互換の実際のまたは偽の Backend であれば何でも試すことができます。
examples.why: 「実際のまたは偽の」 is a literal calque of "real or fake" and reads stiffly; Japanese technical writing uses 実機 for real hardware and フェイク(バックエンド) for the mock provider.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inverted conditions, swapped quantities, dropped negations or hallucinated claims; the protein-folding Δn cancellation argument, the (−1)^k alternation, the 109.5° tetrahedral setup and the Jordan-Wigner one-orbital-per-qubit caveat about parity mapping all survive intact, and core terms are correct and consistent (量子ビット, ハミルトニアン, アンザッツ, パウリ演算子, 生成・消滅演算子, トランスパイル). What a native technical editor would change is register and a few calques: the file opens with keigo ("動画をご覧いただくか", line 10) and again "ご紹介します" (line 23), against the desu/masu-no-keigo convention. "contributions to the Hamiltonian" is rendered 貢献 (line 63) — the physics term is 寄与, which the same file already uses correctly at line 29 ("寄与が少ないハミルトニアン項"), so it is also an internal inconsistency. Two calqued phrasings read as MT rather than written Japanese: "連続した可能性のある位置を占める" (line 65) for "occupy a continuum of possible locations", and "フェルミオン演算子の言語では固有に動作しません" (line 141) for "do not inherently work in the language of fermionic operators". None of these would mislead a learner.

examples.source: Watch the video on mapping from Olivia Lanes, or open the video in a separate window on YouTube.
examples.suggested: Olivia Lanes によるマッピングの動画を視聴するか、YouTube で別ウィンドウとして開いてください。
examples.translation: Olivia Lanes によるマッピングの動画をご覧いただくか、[YouTube] で別ウィンドウとして開いてください。
examples.why: ご覧いただく is keigo, which this locale's convention excludes in favor of plain desu/masu. Same slip at line 23 (『さまざまな角度からご紹介します』 for 'dive into some representative example problems').

examples.source: With this, we will have gathered all the necessary contributions to the Hamiltonian that is necessary to simulate it on a quantum computer.
examples.suggested: これにより、量子コンピュータでシミュレーションするために必要なハミルトニアンへの寄与をすべて揃えたことになります。
examples.translation: これにより、量子コンピュータでシミュレーションするために必要なハミルトニアンへの必要な貢献をすべて収集できます。
examples.why: 貢献 means a person's contribution/service; the physics term for a contribution to a quantity is 寄与, which this same file uses correctly at line 29 (『量子状態の最終エネルギーへの寄与が少ないハミルトニアン項』). Within-file inconsistency plus a slightly wrong register for the domain. The doubled 必要な…必要な also reads redundantly.

examples.source: In real proteins, amino acids can occupy a continuum of possible locations.
examples.suggested: 実際のタンパク質では、アミノ酸が取り得る位置は連続的です。
examples.translation: 実際のタンパク質では、アミノ酸は連続した可能性のある位置を占めることができます。
examples.why: 『連続した可能性のある位置』 is a word-order calque of 'a continuum of possible locations' and parses ambiguously in Japanese (does 連続した modify 可能性 or 位置?). A native writer would attach 連続的 to the set of possible positions.

examples.source: ...quantum computers usually operate in a qubit basis with specific rules for representing fermionic systems; they do not inherently work in the language of fermionic operators.
examples.suggested: ...量子ビット基底で動作します。フェルミオン演算子の言語をそのまま扱えるわけではありません。
examples.translation: ...量子ビット基底で動作します。フェルミオン演算子の言語では固有に動作しません。
examples.why: 『固有に動作しません』 is a literal rendering of 'inherently work' that no Japanese technical writer would produce; 固有に does not collocate with 動作する here. Meaning is still recoverable, so this is stylistic, not misleading.

examples.source: ...we might dictate a cutoff distance below which you consider the pair to be interacting, or you might do something more complicated.
examples.suggested: ...それ以下であればペアが相互作用していると見なすカットオフ距離を設定するか、...
examples.translation: 目的に応じて、ペアが相互作用していると見なすカットオフ距離を設定するか、より複雑な方法を選択するかもしれません。
examples.why: The 'below which' qualifier is dropped, so the translation states only that a cutoff distance exists without saying which side counts as interacting. A reader familiar with cutoffs will infer it, so this is a dropped qualifier rather than an inversion — MINOR, not misleading.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — I checked every prose paragraph including the last 40% (bias-field iteration loop, local-search post-processing, AR definition, seed/transpilation-level notes, Example 3 HUBO reproduction instructions, and the Quipu closing note) and found no inverted condition, swapped quantity, dropped caveat, or hallucinated claim; the tricky items (「約10回の反復」 vs 変分アルゴリズムの「約100回」, 「エネルギーが低い場合、そのビット列が新しい解として採用されます」, 「`direct_qubit_mapping`を`True`に設定」) are all correct. Three editorial defects remain: (1) "classical variables" is rendered as 「Classical変数」 — the English adjective is left glued to a Japanese noun instead of 古典変数; (2) "counterdiabatic" is left as bare English in 「counterdiabatic項」/「counterdiabaticプロトコル」 where Japanese literature uses 反断熱（項/プロトコル）, so the one term that carries the whole compression story is unglossed for a JA reader; (3) the hedge "up to ten times fewer" loses 「最大で」 and becomes the flat 「通常10倍少なく」, slightly firming up a benchmark claim. Register is correct informal です/ます with no keigo (「参照してください」「お試しください」 are fine); nothing here would mislead a learner, so this is not a FAIL despite the fast pass's verdict.

examples.source: The Optimizer uses a 1-to-1 mapping between classical variables and qubits
examples.suggested: Optimizerは古典変数と量子ビット間の1対1マッピングを使用するため
examples.translation: OptimizerはClassical変数と量子ビット間の1対1マッピングを使用するため
examples.why: 「Classical変数」 mixes an untranslated English adjective into a Japanese compound; the established term is 古典変数. Recognizable, so MINOR, but no Japanese technical writer would leave it this way.

examples.source: introducing counterdiabatic terms into the underlying time evolution … By using counterdiabatic protocols
examples.suggested: …反断熱（counterdiabatic）項を導入する … 反断熱プロトコルを使用することで
examples.translation: 量子システムの基本的な時間発展にcounterdiabatic項を導入する … counterdiabaticプロトコルを使用することで
examples.why: The key mechanism term is left as bare lowercase English in both occurrences. It is at least used consistently, but 反断熱 is the conventional Japanese rendering and a first-mention gloss would keep the DCQO acronym connected to the concept.

examples.source: The circuits of the bf-DCQO algorithms typically use up to ten times fewer entangling gates than DQA
examples.suggested: bf-DCQOアルゴリズムの回路は、DQAと比べてエンタングリングゲートが通常最大で10倍少なく
examples.translation: bf-DCQOアルゴリズムの回路は、DQAと比べてエンタングリングゲートが通常10倍少なく
examples.why: "up to" is dropped, turning an upper-bound benchmark claim into a flat typical figure. 「通常」 still hedges it so the reader is not actively misled, but the qualifier should be restored.

editor_note: No misleading content: every load-bearing claim survives intact, including the negation in 「水平線が検出*されなければ*、それは垂直線である」, the 60%→100% accuracy narrative, the "約60%低下" loss comparison, and the caveat that a 6x6 grid 「非クリフォードゲートを使用する回路のシミュレーションが可能な量子ビット数（32）を超えています」. What a native technical editor would still change is consistency and a few stiff spots: "qubit" is 量子ビット throughout but slips to クビット once (「隣接するピクセルに対応するクビット間のこの相関」, ~L172); "training" is split three ways — 訓練精度/訓練セット, トレーニングデータ/トレーニングセット, and 学習データ in the closing summary; "least busy backend" is rendered 最も空いている (L377), the calqued 最もビジーでない (L1055), and 最も混雑していない (L1357). Also 「十分な多くのステップにわたって」 (L764) is ungrammatical (should be 十分に多くの), 「フィーチャーレス」 (L173) is a raw katakana calque for "featureless", and 「$Z$ を選択することに特別な制約はありません」 (L257) renders "nothing unique about choosing Z" as "no special constraint", which blunts the point without inverting it.

examples.source: What attributes of an ansatz would correspond to this correlation between adjacent pixels?
examples.suggested: 隣接するピクセルに対応する量子ビット間のこの相関に、アンザッツのどのような性質が対応するでしょうか？
examples.translation: 隣接するピクセルに対応するクビット間のこの相関にはアンザッツのどのような属性が対応するでしょうか？
examples.why: Single slip to クビット in a file that otherwise uses 量子ビット consistently (including the very next sentence); recognizable but inconsistent.

examples.source: training set / training data / training accuracy
examples.suggested: Pick one — e.g. 訓練データ／訓練セット／訓練精度 — and use it everywhere, including the closing recap.
examples.translation: 訓練精度・訓練セット（L477, L551）／トレーニング用・トレーニングデータ（L97, L704, L764）／学習データ（L1352）
examples.why: Three renderings of the same concept within one lesson; the closing summary uses a fourth-context term (学習データ) for what the body called トレーニングデータ.

examples.source: In this case, we will use the least-busy backend.
examples.suggested: ここでは、最も空いている（混雑していない）バックエンドを使用します。
examples.translation: ここでは、最もビジーでないバックエンドを使用します。
examples.why: 最もビジーでない is a direct calque of "least busy" that a Japanese technical writer would not produce; the same sentence earlier in the file (L377) already uses the natural 最も空いている.

examples.source: This does not appear fully converged, as the loss function has not remained roughly level for substantially many steps.
examples.suggested: 損失関数が十分に多くのステップにわたってほぼ一定の水準を保っていないため、完全には収束していないように見えます。
examples.translation: 損失関数が十分な多くのステップにわたってほぼ一定の水準を保っていないため、完全には収束していないように見えます。
examples.why: 「十分な多くの」 is ungrammatical; the adverbial 十分に is required before 多くの.

examples.source: There is nothing unique about choosing $Z$, but it is well motivated:
examples.suggested: $Z$ を選ぶことに特別な意味があるわけではありませんが、十分に理由のある選択です：
examples.translation: $Z$ を選択することに特別な制約はありませんが、よく動機づけられています：
examples.why: "nothing unique" (other observables would also work) is rendered as "no special constraint", shifting the point from "Z is not the only option" to "nothing restricts you"; the pedagogical intent is blunted, though not inverted.

examples.source: the optimization landscape ... becomes exponentially flat and featureless
examples.suggested: 最適化ランドスケープが指数関数的に平坦で特徴のないものになる現象
examples.translation: 最適化ランドスケープが指数関数的に平坦でフィーチャーレスになる現象
examples.why: フィーチャーレス is an unassimilated katakana calque; 特徴のない is the ordinary Japanese rendering in this context.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inverted conditions, swapped quantities or hallucinated claims; the stochastic-transpiler caveat (「より良い回路が必ずしも見つかるとは限りません」), the SWAP/CX-error warning and the VF2PostLayout conclusion all land correctly, and register is consistent desu/masu with no keigo. What a native editor would change is residual drift from an older English revision: the EN's "supported instruction set" is rendered twice as basis gates (「ネイティブ基底ゲート」 in the Target bullet, 「基底ゲート」 in the "essential pieces of information" sentence) and the section heading "Supported instructions" became 「基底ゲート」, narrowing a deliberately broader term; the same section opens with an addition not in the source, 「_基底ゲート_ と呼ばれる限られた命令セット」. In the same paragraph the EN's `FakeSherbrooke` is replaced by 「_ibm_sherbrooke_」, so the prose names a QPU the surrounding code never instantiates. One sentence is also noticeably calqued: 「任意の量子演算をそれらのゲートに分解できることを意味するユニバーサルゲートセットを提供する、1 量子ビットおよび 2 量子ビットゲートで構成される必要があります」 stacks the whole English relative-clause chain in front of the head noun. None of these would make a learner form a false belief.

examples.source: The `Target` contains all the relevant constraints of a device, such as its supported instruction set, qubit connectivity, and pulse or timing information.
examples.suggested: …には、サポートされる命令セット、量子ビット接続性、パルスやタイミング情報など…
examples.translation: [`Target`] には、ネイティブ基底ゲート、量子ビット接続性、パルスやタイミング情報など、デバイスに関するすべての関連制約が含まれています。
examples.why: "supported instruction set" is narrowed to "native basis gates" (a leftover from an older EN revision). The instruction set includes measure/reset/delay and control-flow ops, not just basis gates — the learner is told the Target holds less than it does. Same substitution recurs at line 101 and in the heading 「基底ゲート」 for "Supported instructions".

examples.source: The default single-qubit gates on `FakeSherbrooke` are `rz`, `x`, and `sx`, and the default two-qubit gate is `ecr` (echoed cross-resonance).
examples.suggested: `FakeSherbrooke` のデフォルトの 1 量子ビットゲートは …
examples.translation: _ibm_sherbrooke_ のデフォルトの 1 量子ビットゲートは `rz`、`x`、`sx` で、デフォルトの 2 量子ビットゲートは `ecr`（エコーされたクロスレゾナンス）です。
examples.why: The prose names ibm_sherbrooke, but every code cell on the page instantiates FakeSherbrooke; the sentence no longer matches its own setup. The statement stays true (the mock mirrors the real device), so it misdirects rather than misleads.

examples.source: Every quantum computer supports a limited instruction set.
examples.suggested: すべての量子コンピューターは、限られた命令セットのみをサポートします。
examples.translation: すべての量子コンピューターは _基底ゲート_ と呼ばれる限られた命令セットをサポートしています。
examples.why: Adds a definitional gloss ("called basis gates") that the English does not make here. The gloss is factually defensible, but it pre-empts the distinction the current EN draws between the instruction set and the basis gates, and it is content the source does not assert.

examples.source: This set should consist of single- and two-qubit gates that provide a universal gate set, meaning that any quantum operation can be decomposed into those gates.
examples.suggested: このセットは、1 量子ビットゲートと 2 量子ビットゲートからなるユニバーサルゲートセットである必要があります。つまり、任意の量子演算をそれらのゲートに分解できるということです。
examples.translation: このセットは、任意の量子演算をそれらのゲートに分解できることを意味するユニバーサルゲートセットを提供する、1 量子ビットおよび 2 量子ビットゲートで構成される必要があります。
examples.why: The English trailing clauses are all stacked before the head noun, producing a 50-character pre-modifier a Japanese technical writer would split into two sentences. Grammatical but audibly machine-translated, and the "meaning that…" intuition gets buried.
