editor_note: No misleading content: the load-bearing technical passages are faithful — the Monte Carlo quadratic-speedup paragraph correctly renders "reduce the error by 1/X requires X² traditional but only X quantum samples" (「誤差を $1/X$ 倍に低減するには、従来の手法では $X^2$ 倍のサンプルが必要ですが、量子サンプルでは $X$ 倍で済みます」) with both interpretations (1)/(2) intact, and domain terms are right (thermodynamic observables→熱力学的観測量, protein folding problem→タンパク質折り畳み問題, quantum kernels→量子カーネル). What a native editor would change: in the long "Distribution and logistics" paragraph the clause「先進企業はビジネス価値を生み出す社内の量子能力を識別・テストするユースケースを模索しています」scrambles the English subject/object (there the companies identify and test the use cases, which in turn generate in-house quantum capability) and injects「ビジネス価値」that actually belongs to the very next sentence, where it is then repeated. 「近期的な技術的実現可能性」uses a Chinese-ism (近期) no Japanese technical writer would use — 短期的な/近い将来の is the natural word. Register slips: the recurring section header「こちらもご確認ください」and「以下のリソースをご確認ください」/「ご存知ですか」use honorific ご- forms against the no-keigo convention, and the bullet lists are stiffly imperative with「…レポートを読んでください：」repeated seven times where a noun-phrase link label would read far better; 「量子コンピューティングのチャンピオン」is a raw calque best glossed as 推進者. (FYI only, outside prose scope: the bp paragraph carries a newsroom hyperlink on「ネットゼロ目標を達成」that has no link in the English source.)

examples.source: In anticipation of commercial quantum computing, leading companies are identifying and testing use cases that generate in-house quantum capabilities. The more effectively designed a use case is, the more likely it will be to deliver business value.
examples.suggested: 商業的な量子コンピューティングの到来を見据えて、先進企業は社内に量子の能力を蓄積できるユースケースを特定し、テストしています。
examples.translation: 商業的な量子コンピューティングの到来を見据えて、先進企業はビジネス価値を生み出す社内の量子能力を識別・テストするユースケースを模索しています。ユースケースの設計が優れているほど、ビジネス価値を提供できる可能性が高まります。
examples.why: Subject/object of the relative clause are swapped: in the English the companies identify and test the use cases (and the use cases generate in-house capability); the Japanese makes the use cases the thing that identifies and tests the capability. 「ビジネス価値」is also injected here even though it is not in this sentence, and it then repeats verbatim in the following sentence.

examples.source: Strategic use cases such as this one attend to near-term technical feasibility
examples.suggested: このような戦略的なユースケースは、短期的な技術的実現可能性に目を向け
examples.translation: このような戦略的なユースケースは、近期的な技術的実現可能性に注目し
examples.why: 「近期的」is not standard Japanese (it is the Chinese 近期); a Japanese technical writer would write 短期的な or 近い将来の. Reads as an unedited MT artifact in an otherwise fluent paragraph.

examples.source: **Check this out**
examples.suggested: **あわせてチェック**（または「関連リソース」）
examples.translation: **こちらもご確認ください**
examples.why: The honorific ご- form (also 「以下のリソースをご確認ください」, 「ご存知ですか」) breaks the file's no-keigo convention; the course register elsewhere is plain desu/masu. Repeated as a section header five times, so the slip is visible throughout.

examples.source: Read the IBM report on exploring quantum use cases for airlines: “Exploring Quantum Computing Use Cases for Airlines.”
examples.suggested: 航空会社向け量子ユースケースに関するIBMのレポート：["Exploring Quantum Computing Use Cases for Airlines."]
examples.translation: IBMの航空会社向け量子ユースケースレポートを読んでください：["Exploring Quantum Computing Use Cases for Airlines."]
examples.why: 「…を読んでください：」/「…を探求してください：」is used seven times across the resource bullets. Japanese documentation conventionally uses a noun-phrase label for link lists rather than a repeated imperative; the calqued colon-plus-imperative pattern reads as English syntax carried over.

examples.source: This can be done by identifying a quantum computing champion
examples.suggested: これは、量子コンピューティングの推進者（チャンピオン）を決めること
examples.translation: これは、量子コンピューティングのチャンピオンを特定すること
examples.why: Business-English "champion" (an internal advocate/sponsor) transliterated bare as 「チャンピオン」reads as a contest winner to a Japanese business reader; 推進者/旗振り役 with the English in parentheses conveys the intended role.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the usage definitions (session = セッションがアクティブな状態の経過時間, batch = 累積時間, single job = ジョブを実行するために QPU がロックされていた時間), the failed/canceled split (system error → ゼロ, user error → その時点までに発生した消費量), the rep_delay trade-off (総実行時間は短縮されますが、状態準備のエラー率が増加する) and the "measurement can take 56 times longer than an x gate" example all land correctly, and register is consistent desu/masu with no keigo. Three things a native technical editor would still change: (1) "circuit" is rendered two ways within the same bullet — Circuit (総長はCircuitによって異なります, 典型的なCircuitの長さ, 追加のCircuitが実行され) vs 回路 (回路全体の長さが増加する, 回路の総時間を返します) — pick one; (2) "qubit-wise commuting observables" uses クビット単位 where the Qiskit-JA convention is 量子ビット単位 (or キュービット); (3) "the last 28 full days" becomes 直近28日分の完全なデータ, which shifts the qualifier from *complete days* to *complete data* (完全な28日分 would be right) — the following clause rescues it, so it is not misleading. Also the emphatic "this is NOT the time used for billing" flattens to a plain これは課金に使用される時間ではありません with no emphasis carried over.

examples.source: the total length varies from circuit to circuit … A typical circuit length is likely between 50-100 microseconds … which would increase the total circuit length
examples.suggested: Use one rendering consistently (e.g. 回路 throughout, or Circuit throughout): 総長は回路によって異なります … 典型的な回路長は … 回路全体の長さが増加することがあります
examples.translation: 総長はCircuitによって異なります … 典型的なCircuitの長さは、50〜100マイクロ秒程度です … 回路全体の長さが増加することがあります
examples.why: Within a single bullet the same concept alternates between Circuit and 回路; a learner cannot tell whether they denote the same thing. Not misleading, but an editor would unify it.

examples.source: Estimator groups qubit-wise commuting observables, which reduces the number of executions.
examples.suggested: Estimator は量子ビット単位で可換な観測量をグループ化するため、実行数を削減できます。
examples.translation: Estimatorはクビット単位で可換な観測量をグループ化するため、実行数を削減できます。
examples.why: クビット is a non-standard transliteration; Japanese Qiskit documentation uses 量子ビット (or キュービット). Recognizable, so minor, but off-convention.

examples.source: The Analytics page usage is re-calculated hourly and includes the last 28 full days
examples.suggested: アナリティクスページの使用量は1時間ごとに再計算され、直近の丸28日分（完全な1日単位の28日間）を対象とします。
examples.translation: アナリティクスページの使用量は1時間ごとに再計算され、直近28日分の完全なデータを含みます。
examples.why: "28 full days" qualifies the days as complete, not the data as complete; the JA reads as a claim about data completeness. The next clause (28日前の00:00から) restores the intent, so it stops short of misleading.

examples.source: returns the total circuit time, but this is NOT the time used for billing.
examples.suggested: 回路の総時間を返しますが、これは課金に使用される時間では**ありません**。
examples.translation: 回路の総時間を返しますが、これは課金に使用される時間ではありません。
examples.why: The English capitalizes NOT to stop a reader from billing off this number; the JA states it flatly and the warning loses its emphasis in a note admonition.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — I checked the risky spots (the N_x < N flip logic, the modified-ReLU δ/h description, the Q3-already-occupied p(flip)=0 example, the "too few samples miss the ground-state support vectors" caveat, the ±1.6 mH chemical-accuracy caveat and the ~24 mH gap) and found no drift, inversion or hallucination. The defects are terminological. "coupled cluster singles and doubles" is rendered 連立クラスター単双励起（CCSD）法 (§1.2); 連立 means "simultaneous" (連立方程式) — the field's term is 結合クラスター, and the same paragraph then switches to 単一励起/二重励起, so 単双 is also internally inconsistent. The file also splits cleanly at §4.2 into a second translation register: 量子ビット→キュービット, ビットストリング→ビット列, コンフィギュレーション回復→配置回復, イテレーション→反復, 平均軌道占有率→平均占有数. Eigensolver gets three renderings (固有値解法器 §4, 固有状態ソルバー §4.1/§4.2, 固有値ソルバー §4.2 option list), and "local unitary coupled cluster Jastrow" loses "coupled" (局所ユニタリークラスター Jastrow) in §1.1. All recognizable; none teaches a false concept.

examples.source: classical coupled cluster singles and doubles (CCSD) method
examples.suggested: 古典的な結合クラスター（CCSD, 一電子・二電子励起）法
examples.translation: 古典的な連立クラスター単双励起（CCSD）法
examples.why: 連立クラスター is not the Japanese term for coupled cluster (連立 = simultaneous, as in 連立方程式); the established rendering is 結合クラスター. The CCSD acronym keeps it recognizable, so this is imperfect rather than misleading, but a chemist would not write 連立クラスター. 単双励起 is also inconsistent with the very next sentence's 単一励起演算子 / 二重励起演算子.

examples.source: Since qubits are indexed from the right of a bitstring in Qiskit, column 0 represents qubit N-1
examples.suggested: Qiskit ではビットストリングの右側から量子ビットがインデックスされるため、列 ``0`` は量子ビット ``N-1`` に対応し
examples.translation: Qiskitではビット列の右側からキュービットがインデックスされるため、列 ``0`` はキュービット ``N-1`` に対応し
examples.why: Sections 1–4.1 consistently use 量子ビット and ビットストリング (e.g. §1 「各スピン軌道を1つの量子ビットで表します」, 「ビットストリング、配置、行列式という用語を互換的に使用します」); from §4.2 onward the file switches to キュービット and ビット列. Same concept, two vocabularies in one lesson — the classic two-pass-merge split.

examples.source: iterations: Number of self-consistent configuration recovery iterations / after a few iterations
examples.suggested: ``iterations``：自己無撞着コンフィギュレーション回復のイテレーション回数 / 数回のイテレーション後に
examples.translation: ``iterations``：自己無撞着な配置回復の反復回数 / 数回の反復後に
examples.why: The named procedure is コンフィギュレーション回復 everywhere in §1–§4.1 (heading 4.1 included) and イテレーション is used for the loop counter; §4.2/§4.3 rename them 配置回復 and 反復. A learner scanning for the section that explains ``iterations`` has to map two labels onto one concept. 平均軌道占有率 likewise becomes 平均占有数 in §4.3.

examples.source: Eigensolver / eigenstate solver / eigensolver
examples.suggested: pick one, e.g. 固有状態ソルバー throughout (with 固有値ソルバー only where the English says eigensolver)
examples.translation: 固有値解法器 / 固有状態ソルバー / 固有値ソルバー
examples.why: Three distinct renderings of the same component within one file, including 固有値解法器 which no Japanese quantum-chemistry writer would use. Recognizable, so MINOR, but it reads as unedited.

examples.source: which are used in the post-processing routine / The self-consistent configuration routine
examples.suggested: 後処理ルーチン / 自己無撞着コンフィギュレーション回復ルーチン
examples.translation: これが後処理ルーティンで使用されます / 自己無撞着コンフィギュレーションルーティン
examples.why: In Japanese technical writing the loanword for a code routine is ルーチン; ルーティン is the everyday-habit sense (ルーティンワーク). Small but it flags the text as translated rather than written.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inverted conditions, dropped caveats or hallucinations; the tricky bits (resilience level 0 turning off `zne_mitigation` but being overridden by an explicit `= True`, "제로 편향이 보장되지는 않습니다", "특정 노이즈 관리 방법이 각 복원력 수준에서 적용된다는 보장이 없습니다", and the partial negation "모든 옵션이 모든 유형의 Circuit에서 함께 작동하지는 않습니다") are all rendered correctly. What a native technical editor would still change is terminology: "dynamical decoupling" is rendered "동적 분리" ("dynamic separation"), where the field uses "동적 디커플링" (or 동적 결합 해제) — 분리 loses the decoupling sense; and "readout error" is rendered "읽기 오류" ("read error") instead of the conventional 판독 오류, both in the table cell and inside "트월된 읽기 오류 소거 (TREX)". Separately, lowercase statistical "estimators" in the level-2 row was capitalized into the primitive name ("일반적으로 Estimator의 편향을 줄이지만"), narrowing a general statement about estimators to the Estimator primitive — harmless in this page's context but not what the source says. Register (합니다체 declaratives + ~하세요 imperatives) is consistent house style and reads naturally; "트월링/트월된" is used consistently.

examples.source: dynamical decoupling
examples.suggested: 동적 디커플링
examples.translation: 동적 분리
examples.why: '분리' means separation; the standard Korean rendering of decoupling in quantum-control contexts is 디커플링 (or 결합 해제). As written a learner may not connect the bullet to the DynamicalDecouplingOptions API it links to.

examples.source: Mitigate error associated with readout errors / Twirled Readout Error eXtinction (TREX)
examples.suggested: 판독 오류와 관련된 오류 완화 / 트월된 판독 오류 소거 (TREX)
examples.translation: 읽기 오류와 관련된 오류 완화 / 트월된 읽기 오류 소거 (TREX)
examples.why: '읽기 오류' reads as a generic 'read error' (file/disk sense); the conventional domain term for measurement readout error is 판독 오류. Recognizable but literal-and-loose.

examples.source: Typically reduces bias in estimators, but is not guaranteed to be zero-bias.
examples.suggested: 일반적으로 추정량의 편향을 줄이지만 제로 편향이 보장되지는 않습니다.
examples.translation: 일반적으로 Estimator의 편향을 줄이지만 제로 편향이 보장되지는 않습니다.
examples.why: Lowercase 'estimators' here is the statistical sense (estimated quantities), not the Qiskit Estimator primitive; capitalizing it narrows a general statistical claim to the primitive. Not misleading in this page's context, but it is not what the source states.

editor_note: One genuine quantity drift makes the simulator section teach a false scale: "several orders of magnitude more bits ... than are estimated to be available in all existing classical storage media on Earth" is rendered "지구상의 모든 기존 고전 저장 매체에서 사용 가능한 것으로 추정되는 디지털 정보 비트보다 수십 배 더 많습니다" — "수십 배" means "tens of times", not "몇 자릿수/수십 자릿수" (orders of magnitude). This is the load-bearing sentence for why a classical simulator can never run an industry-useful quantum calculation; a learner told 10^30 bits is only ~tens of times Earth's total storage would conclude the gap is nearly closable, the opposite of the lesson. Beyond that the prose is faithful but carries several literal calques a Korean technical editor would rewrite: "yesterday's game-changing technologies" → "전날의 게임 체인저 기술" (전날 = the previous day, not "past"), "near-term" → "근처 기간의", "largest fleet of quantum computers" → "가장 많은 양자 컴퓨터 함대" (함대 = naval fleet), "Join quantum's inner circle" → "양자의 내부 원 참여", and "with foresight" → "원견지명" which is not a Korean word (선견지명 is). Register is 합니다체 throughout with one stray 해요체 ("참여하길 바라요") at the Responsible Quantum Computing close.

examples.source: This is several orders of magnitude more bits of digital information than are estimated to be available in all existing classical storage media on Earth.
examples.suggested: 이는 지구상의 모든 기존 고전 저장 매체에 존재한다고 추정되는 디지털 정보의 비트 수보다 몇 자릿수(수십억 배 이상)나 더 많은 양입니다.
examples.translation: 이것은 지구상의 모든 기존 고전 저장 매체에서 사용 가능한 것으로 추정되는 디지털 정보 비트보다 수십 배 더 많습니다.
examples.why: Swapped quantity: 'several orders of magnitude' (≥10^3, in fact ~10^8 here) becomes '수십 배' = tens of times. The whole point of item (2) is that the storage requirement is unreachably beyond all classical storage on Earth; '수십 배' makes the gap sound like an engineering increment, so the learner draws the opposite conclusion about whether simulators could ever scale.

examples.source: Many businesses would leap at the chance to go back in time to capitalize early on yesterday’s game-changing technologies, such as the internet.
examples.suggested: 많은 기업은 인터넷처럼 과거에 판도를 바꾼 기술을 초기에 선점하기 위해 시간을 되돌릴 기회를 간절히 바랍니다.
examples.translation: 많은 기업은 인터넷과 같은 전날의 게임 체인저 기술을 조기에 활용하기 위해 과거로 돌아갈 수 있는 기회를 간절히 원합니다.
examples.why: '전날의' literally means 'of the previous day' — a mistranslation of the idiomatic 'yesterday's' (= past era). Opening sentence of the module, and no Korean technical writer would write 전날의 게임 체인저 기술.

examples.source: Explore use cases with foresight.
examples.suggested: 선견지명을 가지고 사용 사례를 탐색합니다.
examples.translation: 원견지명으로 사용 사례를 탐색합니다.
examples.why: '원견지명' is not a Korean word; the established four-character idiom is 선견지명. One of IBM's five stated responsibility principles, so it reads as a typo in a memorized list.

examples.source: Could be explored with a near-term classical-quantum hybrid approach.
examples.suggested: – 단기적으로 실현 가능한 고전-양자 하이브리드 접근 방식으로 탐색할 수 있습니다.
examples.translation: – 근처 기간의 고전-양자 하이브리드 접근 방식으로 탐색할 수 있습니다.
examples.why: '근처 기간의' is a word-for-word calque of 'near-term' (근처 = nearby in space). The field's normal rendering is 단기/근시일 내.

examples.source: the largest fleet of quantum computers … Join quantum’s inner circle
examples.suggested: 가장 많은 양자 컴퓨터를 보유 … 양자 분야의 핵심 그룹에 합류하기
examples.translation: 가장 많은 양자 컴퓨터 함대 … 양자의 내부 원 참여
examples.why: 함대 is a naval fleet and 내부 원 is a geometric circle; both are literal renderings of English figurative usage and read as machine output in a business-audience module.

editor_note: No misleading drift: the two primitive definitions ("Estimator는 양자 Circuit으로 준비된 상태에 대한 관측 가능량의 기댓값을 계산합니다" / "Sampler는 ... 출력 레지스터를 샘플링합니다"), the abstraction-ladder pair ("하드웨어에 가까울수록 더 낮은 수준의 추상화가 필요합니다"), and the supersession claim about `backend.run` are all faithful, and 기댓값/관측 가능량/상태벡터/오류 완화 are the correct conventional Korean terms used consistently. Three things a native technical editor would still change. (1) In "Benefits", the English hedge "you *might be able to* more easily access advanced hardware capabilities" is flattened to the flat assertion "더 쉽게 접근할 수 있습니다", and the comparative "a *more* 'out-of-the-box' way" loses its "더" as well. (2) "implementing primitives natively" is rendered "프리미티브를 기본적으로 구현하면", where 기본적으로 reads as "basically / by default" rather than "natively" (네이티브로/자체적으로) — recognizable but wrong-sounding to an engineer. (3) "would not and should not be familiar with distilling such raw data into 0s and 1s" collapses into two near-identical clauses ("알지 못해도 되고 알 필요도 없다"), losing the descriptive half ("most developers are not familiar with it"). Register is uniform 합니다체 with 해요체 headings/imperatives — a defensible standard for Korean technical docs, not counted as a defect.

examples.source: because of the additional layer of abstraction, you might be able to more easily access advanced hardware capabilities of a given provider
examples.suggested: 추가적인 추상화 계층 덕분에 특정 제공업체의 고급 하드웨어 기능에 더 쉽게 접근할 수도 있습니다
examples.translation: 추가적인 추상화 계층으로 인해 특정 제공업체의 고급 하드웨어 기능에 더 쉽게 접근할 수 있습니다
examples.why: The English modal hedge "might be able to" is dropped, turning a possibility into a flat guarantee. A dropped qualifier, not a false claim, so MINOR.

examples.source: For hardware providers, implementing primitives natively means you can provide your users with a more "out-of-the-box" way to access your hardware features
examples.suggested: 하드웨어 제공업체의 경우, 프리미티브를 네이티브로 직접 구현하면 ... 더 "즉시 사용 가능한" 방법을 사용자에게 제공할 수 있습니다
examples.translation: 하드웨어 제공업체의 경우, 프리미티브를 기본적으로 구현하면 ... "즉시 사용 가능한" 방법을 사용자에게 제공할 수 있습니다
examples.why: 기본적으로 means "basically / by default", not "natively"; the intended sense is a first-party in-house implementation. The comparative "a more out-of-the-box way" also loses its 더.

examples.source: Acknowledging that most developers would not and should not be familiar with distilling such raw data into 0s and 1s
examples.suggested: 대부분의 개발자는 이러한 원시 데이터를 0과 1로 정제하는 데 익숙하지도 않고 익숙할 필요도 없다는 점을 인식하여
examples.translation: 대부분의 개발자들이 이러한 원시 데이터를 0과 1로 변환하는 방법을 알지 못해도 되고 알 필요도 없다는 점을 인식하여
examples.why: "알지 못해도 되고" and "알 필요도 없다" say the same thing twice; the descriptive half of the English pair ("would not be familiar") disappears, leaving a tautological, slightly stiff clause.

editor_note: The proof chain (Schmidt decomposition, unitary equivalence, bit-commitment impossibility, Hughston-Jozsa-Wootters) is faithful and reads naturally, with no hallucinated claims and no inverted conditions — but three core terms are split within the file. "Partial trace" is 부분 추적 at lines 70 and 492 yet becomes 편미분 트레이스 ("partial-DERIVATIVE trace") at line 233; "purification" is 정화 throughout but slips to 순수화 (lines 121, 137) and 순화 (line 141); "reduced state" is 축소 상태 in the Schmidt section but 환원 상태 at lines 396 and 475 (plus 스펙트럼 분해 vs 스펙트럴 분해 at line 343). Separately, the sufficiency condition at line 42 drops "at least": EN "if Y has at least as many classical states as X" becomes "Y가 X만큼의 고전 상태를 가진다면", which reads as an exact-equality requirement and understates the generality (the following sentence about fewer states keeps it from being outright false). One sentence (line 216) is a stacked-relative-clause monster that a native technical editor would split. None of this teaches a false concept, so MINOR rather than FAIL.

examples.source: To see that the unique collection … is necessarily orthogonal, we can begin by computing the partial trace.
examples.suggested: … 부분 추적(partial trace)을 계산하는 것부터 시작할 수 있습니다.
examples.translation: … 반드시 직교함을 보이기 위해, 편미분 트레이스를 계산하는 것부터 시작할 수 있습니다.
examples.why: 편미분 is the standard Korean term for a PARTIAL DERIVATIVE; "편미분 트레이스" names an operation that does not exist. The same file correctly uses 부분 추적 at lines 70 and 492, so this is a one-off wrong term inside an otherwise consistent file.

examples.source: is therefore a purification of ρ. / Schmidt decompositions are closely connected with purifications
examples.suggested: 는 따라서 $\rho$의 정화입니다. / 슈미트 분해는 정화(purification)와 밀접하게 연관되어 있으며
examples.translation: 는 따라서 $\rho$의 순수화입니다. / 슈미트 분해는 순화(purification)와 밀접하게 연관되어 있으며
examples.why: The lesson's headline concept is defined as 정화 in the definition box and used that way ~20 times; the worked Example section switches to 순수화 twice and the Schmidt intro to 순화 once. The learner sees three names for the term the whole lesson is about.

examples.source: the reduced state of Bob's qubit B is the completely mixed state / any way of thinking about the reduced state of the first system
examples.suggested: … 축소 상태는 … / 첫 번째 시스템의 축소 상태를
examples.translation: 밥의 qubit $\mathsf{B}$의 환원 상태는 완전 혼합 상태입니다 / 첫 번째 시스템의 환원 상태를
examples.why: "Reduced state" is glossed and used as 축소 상태(reduced state) throughout the Schmidt-decomposition section (lines 217, 265, 306, 308, 312, 314); the last 40% switches to 환원 상태 without warning.

examples.source: In particular, if Y has at least as many classical states as X, then a purification of this form necessarily exists for every state ρ.
examples.suggested: 특히, $\mathsf{Y}$가 $\mathsf{X}$와 같거나 더 많은 수의 고전 상태를 가진다면, …
examples.translation: 특히, $\mathsf{Y}$가 $\mathsf{X}$만큼의 고전 상태를 가진다면, 모든 상태 $\rho$에 대해 이런 형태의 정화가 반드시 존재합니다.
examples.why: "at least as many" is flattened to plain "as many", turning a lower-bound sufficiency condition into an apparent exact-count requirement; a learner would not see that a larger Y also works.

examples.source: For a given basis {|x₀⟩,…} of the vector space corresponding to X, the uniquely determined vectors |z₀⟩,…,|z_{n-1}⟩ for which equation (1) is satisfied won't necessarily satisfy any special properties, even if {|x₀⟩,…} happens to be an orthonormal basis.
examples.suggested: … 방정식 $(1)$을 만족하는 벡터 $\vert z_0\rangle,\ldots$은 유일하게 결정되지만, 설령 $\{\vert x_0\rangle,\ldots\}$이 정규직교 기저라 하더라도 특별한 성질을 만족한다는 보장은 없습니다.
examples.translation: … 방정식 $(1)$을 만족하는 유일하게 결정된 벡터들 $\vert z_0\rangle,\ldots$이 $\{\vert x_0\rangle,\ldots\}$이 정규직교 기저인 경우에도 특별한 성질을 반드시 만족하지는 않습니다.
examples.why: Two subject clauses collide back-to-back (…벡터들이 …기저인 경우에도), a calque of the English relative-clause stack; a Korean technical writer would break the concession off with 설령 … 하더라도 and split the sentence.

editor_note: Meaning is fully faithful — the CX control/target assignment (왼쪽 Qubit이 제어, 오른쪽 Qubit이 대상), the spin-context caveat, and the right-to-left 0-indexed qubit numbering all match the English exactly, and core terms (텐서곱, 상태 벡터, 부분 측정, 메서드, 인자) are correct and consistent. Three surface-level items remain: two humble/honorific 드리 forms ("명확히 말씀드리면", "보여드리기 위해") break the stated 해요체/plain-폐쇄 convention; "다시, 벡터의 경우와 마찬가지로" is a literal calque of sentence-initial "Again," which Korean does not use that way; and "인자는 오른쪽의 텐서 인수로 해석됩니다" collides 인자(argument) with 인수(factor) in one short sentence, muddying which object becomes the right-hand tensor factor. None of these would mislead a learner about the physics or the API.

examples.source: To be clear, this is a $CX$ operation for which the left-hand qubit is the control and the right-hand qubit is the target.
examples.suggested: 분명히 말하면, 이것은 왼쪽 Qubit이 제어이고 오른쪽 Qubit이 대상인 $CX$ 연산입니다.
examples.translation: 명확히 말씀드리면, 이것은 왼쪽 Qubit이 제어이고 오른쪽 Qubit이 대상인 $CX$ 연산입니다.
examples.why: 말씀드리다 is the humble (겸양) form the file's register convention excludes; the same slip recurs at line ~164 as '보여드리기 위해' (→ '보여주기 위해'). Content is correct — control/target are not inverted.

examples.source: Again, like in the vector case, the `^` operation is equivalent.
examples.suggested: 이번에도 벡터의 경우와 마찬가지로 `^` 연산을 똑같이 쓸 수 있습니다.
examples.translation: 다시, 벡터의 경우와 마찬가지로 `^` 연산은 동등합니다.
examples.why: Sentence-initial '다시,' is a word-for-word calque of English 'Again,'. In Korean 다시 means 'once more / repeat the action', so as a discourse connective it reads as machine output; 이번에도 / 앞서와 마찬가지로 is what a native technical writer uses.

examples.source: The argument is interpreted as the tensor factor on the right.
examples.suggested: 인자로 전달한 벡터는 오른쪽 텐서 인자가 됩니다.
examples.translation: 인자는 오른쪽의 텐서 인수로 해석됩니다.
examples.why: 인자 (argument) and 인수 (factor) are near-synonyms in Korean programming usage, so putting both in one seven-word sentence obscures the point that the passed-in Statevector lands on the right side of the tensor product. Recognizable, not wrong — but a native editor would disambiguate.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no dropped caveats: both "queuing time does not decrease for the first job" notes, the Open Plan restriction, the maximum-TTL/cost-limit clause in step 4, and the reactivation caveat ("Zadanie musi przejść przez normalną kolejkę") all land correctly, and the informal "ty" register ("twoje zadania", "znajdziesz", "podaj") is consistent. The defects are stylistic. The batch-threading paragraph nominalizes the English verb into a broken subject — "System zrównoleglenia lub wątkowania kroków wstępnego przetwarzania ... pozwala na ... a następnie uruchamia ..." — which no Polish technical writer would produce (the source says the system parallelizes/threads, not that a "parallelization-or-threading system" allows something), and the same sentence carries the calque "w szybkiej kolejności" for "in quick succession". In the Job mode section, "Pojedyncze żądanie prymitywne" reads as "a crude/primitive request" rather than "a request to a primitive"; the noun form "prymitywu" used two sentences later is the right one.

examples.source: The system parallelizes or threads the pre-processing (classical computing) step of each primitive job to more tightly package quantum execution across jobs, and then runs the quantum execution of each job in quick succession to deliver the most efficient results.
examples.suggested: System zrównolegla lub wątkuje krok wstępnego przetwarzania (obliczenia klasyczne) każdego zadania prymitywu, aby ściślej upakować wykonanie kwantowe wielu zadań, a następnie uruchamia wykonanie kwantowe każdego z nich jedno po drugim w krótkich odstępach, dostarczając możliwie najwydajniejsze wyniki.
examples.translation: System zrównoleglenia lub wątkowania kroków wstępnego przetwarzania (obliczenia klasyczne) każdego zadania prymitywnego pozwala na ściślejsze pakowanie wykonania kwantowego między zadaniami, a następnie uruchamia wykonanie kwantowe każdego zadania w szybkiej kolejności, dostarczając jak najwydajniejsze wyniki.
examples.why: The English finite verb ('the system parallelizes or threads') is turned into a noun-phrase subject ('System zrównoleglenia lub wątkowania ... pozwala'), leaving the following clause 'a następnie uruchamia' hanging off the wrong subject. Meaning survives, so it does not mislead, but it reads as raw MT in the file's densest technical paragraph.

examples.source: A single primitive request made without a context manager.
examples.suggested: Pojedyncze żądanie do prymitywu złożone bez menedżera kontekstu.
examples.translation: Pojedyncze żądanie prymitywne złożone bez menedżera kontekstu.
examples.why: As an adjective, 'prymitywny' in Polish means crude/rudimentary, so 'żądanie prymitywne' reads as 'a crude request' rather than 'a request to a primitive'. The file already uses the correct noun form two sentences later ('podczas tworzenia instancji prymitywu'), so this is also an internal inconsistency.

examples.source: runs the quantum execution of each job in quick succession
examples.suggested: uruchamia wykonanie kwantowe kolejnych zadań w krótkich odstępach czasu
examples.translation: uruchamia wykonanie kwantowe każdego zadania w szybkiej kolejności
examples.why: 'w szybkiej kolejności' is a word-for-word calque of 'in quick succession'; Polish idiom expresses this as 'jedno po drugim' / 'w krótkich odstępach czasu'. Understandable, but a native technical editor would rewrite it.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no dropped caveats, no hallucination: the 2% depolarizing / 5% readout-flip figures, the "50 to 100 qubits" feasibility bound, the "up to global phase" qualifier (z dokładnością do globalnej fazy) and the "very likely to be 0" hedge (najprawdopodobniej wyniesie 0) all survive intact, and the informal "ty" register holds (Zauważ, Załóżmy, chcesz). Terminology is correct and consistent (kubit, bramka, obwód stabilizatorowy, prymityw Sampler/Estimator, wartość oczekiwana obserwabli, błąd depolaryzujący, błąd odczytu). What a native technical editor would still change is a handful of calqued constructions: "obwód jest zagwarantowany jako stabilizatorowy" (line ~72) is English "guaranteed to be" transplanted whole; "nawet wysoko wydajnego symulatora jak Qiskit Aer" (line ~70) needs "wysokowydajnego … takiego jak"; "wchodzi w tę kategorię" (line ~105) should be "należy do tej kategorii". None of these mislead, so they cap the verdict at MINOR_ISSUES.

examples.source: using parameters chosen randomly such that the circuit is guaranteed to be a stabilizer circuit
examples.suggested: używając parametrów wybranych losowo tak, aby obwód z pewnością był obwodem stabilizatorowym
examples.translation: używając parametrów wybranych losowo tak, że obwód jest zagwarantowany jako stabilizatorowy
examples.why: "jest zagwarantowany jako" is a direct calque of "is guaranteed to be"; Polish does not use gwarantować in this predicative-adjective frame. Meaning is preserved, phrasing is not native.

examples.source: would generally exceed the capabilities of even a high-performance simulator like Qiskit Aer
examples.suggested: zwykle przekraczałby możliwości nawet tak wysokowydajnego symulatora jak Qiskit Aer
examples.translation: generalnie przekraczałby możliwości nawet wysoko wydajnego symulatora jak Qiskit Aer
examples.why: "wysoko wydajnego" should be the single compound "wysokowydajnego", and the comparative needs "takiego jak" — bare "symulatora jak X" is English syntax. "generalnie" is also an anglicism here; "zwykle"/"na ogół" is the technical-writing choice.

examples.source: you can run circuits on the quantum computer that have a similar structure to your desired circuit
examples.suggested: możesz uruchamiać na komputerze kwantowym obwody o strukturze podobnej do pożądanego obwodu
examples.translation: możesz uruchamiać obwody na komputerze kwantowym, które mają podobną strukturę do pożądanego obwodu

editor_note: No semantic drift, hallucination or dropped caveat anywhere: the experimental-ABI warning, the "v2.4.0 build works with v2.4.1 but may break on v2.5.0" example, the borrow semantics of `qk_*_convert_from_python` ("Essas funções _emprestam_ o objeto nativo em C…"), and the `PyInit__core` double-underscore rule are all rendered faithfully, and the informal "você" register holds throughout. What a native technical editor would still change: "que muta o DAG no lugar" (line ~412) is a raw calque of "mutates the DAG in place" — "mutar" is not used transitively this way in PT technical prose ("modifica o DAG in place" / "altera o próprio DAG"). editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: every paragraph, including the Credly privacy notice at the end, tracks the English faithfully, register is informal "você" throughout, and the topic list (Hamiltonianos / Ansätze / otimizadores clássicos / energias do estado fundamental / comprimentos de ligação) is correct. Three editorial slips remain. (1) Line 12 "Bem-vindo ao **Química quântica com VQE**" mismatches the masculine article with a feminine course name — a native writer would put "Bem-vindo ao curso **Química quântica com VQE**" or "Bem-vindo à ..." (the sibling course page uses "Bem-vindo a *Fundamentos da informação quântica*"). This is consistent across the whole quantum-chem-with-vqe directory (ansatz.mdx, introduction.mdx), so it is an established convention and any fix should be corpus-wide, not local. examples.source: Welcome to **Quantum chemistry with VQE**.

examples.translation: Portanto, o uso continua a acumular após o término de uma sessão caso o QPU ainda esteja executando um job.
examples.why: "Acumular" used intransitively is an English calque; Portuguese requires the pronominal "acumular-se" or the gerund. Meaning is unaffected.

examples.translation: Em geral, se cada um dos seus jobs consome menos de um minuto de tempo de QPU, considere combiná-los em um job maior
examples.why: A hypothetical 'se' clause governing an imperative main clause takes the future subjunctive in standard Portuguese; the present indicative reads as translated-from-English.

editor_note: Há uma inversão direcional que engana o aprendiz: no §4.3 o inglês "left-most (or bottom-most, in the column labels)" foi traduzido duas vezes na mesma frase como "mais à esquerda (ou mais acima…)" / "mais à esquerda e mais acima" — "bottom-most" virou "mais acima" (topo). Como os rótulos do plot_histogram aparecem rotacionados, o caractere de cima corresponde a q0 (que vale 1 em resultados como '001' e '011'), não a q2; seguindo a instrução em PT o leitor olha o bit errado e concluiria que o teletransporte falhou, contradizendo a frase seguinte ("100% de chance de medir q2 no estado |0⟩"). Além disso, o termo central está dividido dentro do arquivo: "Teleportação/teleportação" no título, frontmatter e §1 (linhas 2–4, 17, 32) e "teletransporte/teletransportar" de §4 em diante (linhas 377–969); e o curso referenciado aparece traduzido em §1 ("Fundamentos de Informação Quântica", l.37) mas em inglês em §4.1 ("Basics of Quantum Information", l.396). Fora isso o texto é fiel, natural e com terminologia correta (porta, base computacional, entrelaçamento, matriz de densidade, tomografia de estado quântico, primitivo Sampler), e as tabelas de correção X/Z do teletransporte e da codificação superdensa conferem com o inglês.

examples.source: Recall that in little endian notation, qubit 2 is the left-most (or bottom-most, in the column labels) qubit. Note that the left- and bottom-most qubit in the column labels is a 0 for all possible outcomes.
examples.suggested: Lembre-se de que na notação little endian, o qubit 2 é o qubit mais à esquerda (ou o mais abaixo, nos rótulos de coluna). Note que o qubit mais à esquerda e mais abaixo nos rótulos de coluna é 0 para todos os resultados possíveis.
examples.translation: Lembre-se de que na notação little endian, o qubit 2 é o qubit mais à esquerda (ou mais acima, nos rótulos de coluna). Note que o qubit mais à esquerda e mais acima nos rótulos de coluna é 0 para todos os resultados possíveis.
examples.why: "bottom-most" foi invertido para "mais acima" (duas vezes na mesma frase). Nos rótulos rotacionados do histograma, o caractere de cima corresponde a q0 — que vale 1 em '001' e '011' — de modo que quem seguir a instrução em PT lerá o bit errado e concluirá, erradamente, que o protocolo de teletransporte não funcionou.

examples.source: Quantum teleportation
examples.suggested: Unificar em um único termo em todo o arquivo — p.ex. "teleportação quântica"/"teleportar" — inclusive nos títulos das seções 4 a 4.5 e no resumo.

editor_note: Semantically faithful throughout — no drift, no hallucination, no inverted or softened claims; the noise-management paragraph ("equilíbrio entre aperfeiçoar seus resultados e garantir que seu job seja concluído em um tempo razoável") tracks the English exactly, and domain terms are conventional and consistent (desacoplamento dinâmico, twirling de Pauli, mitigação e supressão de erros, Sampler/backend/job kept in English as the field does). Informal register holds; no formal-address slips. The one thing a native technical editor would change: the cross-reference "See the [feature compatibility table] guide" is rendered as "Veja o [guia de compatibilidade de recursos]", which drops the word "tabela" even though the link anchor (#options-compatibility-table) lands on a table — the reader is pointed at a guide rather than the table itself. Not misleading, just a lost specifier; "Veja a [tabela de compatibilidade de recursos]" would restore it.

examples.suggested: Veja a [tabela de compatibilidade de recursos](/guides/sampler-options#options-compatibility-table) para detalhes completos.
examples.translation: Veja o [guia de compatibilidade de recursos](/guides/sampler-options#options-compatibility-table) para detalhes completos.
examples.why: The English link text names a specific table (and the anchor targets it); the Portuguese renames the target a 'guia' and drops 'tabela', so the reader is not told they are being sent to a compatibility table. Minor loss of pointer specificity, not a meaning change.

editor_note: The prose is otherwise fluent, natural and faithful (informal "você" holds; "vetor de estado", "medição na base padrão", "a menos de uma fase global", "lei dos grandes números" are all correct and consistent), but two sentences assert things the English does not and would actively mislead a learner. (1) Line 85: the English says matrix multiplication "can be performed using the `@` operator"; the Portuguese says "usando a função `matmul` do `NumPy`" — the very next code cell uses `@`, so the example no longer matches its own setup and the learner is pointed at a function the lesson never shows. (2) Line 262: the English references `array_to_latex` (the function imported and used a few cells above); the Portuguese invents `array_from_latex`, a name that does not exist in Qiskit. (3) Line 338 leaves "descritas pelo Circuit" where the source says "described by the circuit" — an untranslated stray that reads as a class name rather than the ordinary noun "circuito" used everywhere else in the file.

examples.source: Matrix multiplication, including matrix-vector multiplication as a special case, can be performed using the `@` operator.
examples.suggested: A multiplicação de matrizes, incluindo a multiplicação matriz-vetor como caso especial, pode ser realizada usando o operador `@`.
examples.translation: A multiplicação de matrizes, incluindo a multiplicação matriz-vetor como caso especial, pode ser realizada usando a função `matmul` do `NumPy`.
examples.why: Substitutes a different API for the one being taught. The immediately following code cell (`M1 @ ket1`, `M1 @ M2`, `M @ M`) demonstrates the `@` operator, so the sentence no longer matches the example it introduces and teaches the learner the wrong construct.

examples.source: Note that the `latex` option produces results equivalent to `array_to_latex`.
examples.suggested: Note que a opção `latex` produz resultados equivalentes ao `array_to_latex`.
examples.translation: Note que a opção `latex` produz resultados equivalentes ao `array_from_latex`.
examples.why: Hallucinated identifier: `array_from_latex` does not exist. The function actually imported earlier in this same lesson is `array_to_latex`; a learner following the text would get an ImportError and lose the cross-reference to the earlier section.

examples.source: We can also initialize a starting quantum state vector and then evolve that state according to the sequence of operations described by the circuit.
examples.suggested: ... de acordo com a sequência de operações descritas pelo circuito.
examples.translation: Também podemos inicializar um vetor de estado quântico inicial e então evoluir esse estado de acordo com a sequência de operações descritas pelo Circuit.
examples.why: Untranslated stray capitalized 'Circuit' where the plain noun is meant; every other occurrence in the file uses 'circuito' / 'circuitos quânticos', so the reader may mistake it for the `QuantumCircuit` class name rather than the circuit just built.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: every factual claim matches the source (120 qubits/r1 Nighthawk, 156/133 qubits Heron, dezembro de 2025, julho de 2024, "rede hexagonal pesada" for heavy-hex, "mitigação de TLS", "trocas entre diferentes atributos" for tradeoffs), and the informal "você" register holds in the Admonition. Two spots are stiff, calqued adjective placement that a native technical editor would reorder: in the Heron paragraph, "o controle de dois qubits e de qubit único rápido e de alta fidelidade" strands "rápido e de alta fidelidade" after "qubit único", so the qualifiers read as attaching only to single-qubit control instead of to the control as a whole; and in the Nighthawk paragraph "cargas de trabalho de aplicações aprimoradas" lets "aprimoradas" attach to "aplicações" rather than to the workloads, as in the English "enhanced application workloads". Neither would mislead a learner about the hardware — both are fluency/attachment slips, not meaning changes.

examples.source: The signals required to enable the fast, high-fidelity two-qubit and single-qubit control are delivered with high-density flex cabling.
examples.suggested: Os sinais necessários para permitir o controle rápido e de alta fidelidade de dois qubits e de um único qubit são entregues por meio de cabos flexíveis de alta densidade.
examples.translation: Os sinais necessários para permitir o controle de dois qubits e de qubit único rápido e de alta fidelidade são entregues por meio de cabos flexíveis de alta densidade.
examples.why: Calqued English adjective order: 'rápido e de alta fidelidade' ends up dangling after 'qubit único', so it reads as qualifying only single-qubit control. Moving the adjectives before the two coordinated complements is what a Portuguese technical writer would do and restores the shared scope.

examples.source: ...with increased connectivity for enhanced application workloads.
examples.suggested: ...com maior conectividade para cargas de trabalho de aplicações mais exigentes / para cargas de trabalho de aplicação aprimoradas.
examples.translation: ...com maior conectividade para cargas de trabalho de aplicações aprimoradas.
examples.why: 'aprimoradas' sits next to 'aplicações' and is naturally parsed as 'enhanced applications'; in the English 'enhanced' qualifies the workloads. Not misleading about the hardware, but the attachment is off and the phrase reads as machine-order Portuguese.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination found: every technical claim (EPLG/CLOPS definitions, circuit-depth game, resilience levels 0/1/2, ZNE "adicionamos ruído em cima do que já existe", PEC being a manual opt-in rather than resilience level 3, PEA "ainda não está disponível no Qiskit") matches the English exactly, and the informal "você" register holds throughout. The defects are wording, not meaning: "on-premises systems" is calqued as "sistemas dedicados em premissas", which is meaningless in Portuguese ("premissas" = logical premises, not physical facilities); "expectation value" is rendered as "valor de expectativa" (lines 92, 147, 159) instead of the standard Portuguese physics term "valor esperado" — recognizable but non-conventional, and at least it is used consistently. Smaller slips: Sampler/Estimator appear lowercase as "o sampler e o estimator" in the primitives intro but capitalized "o Sampler e o Estimator" in the Execute section, and a couple of stiff calques ("qubits suficientes de qualidade alta o suficiente", "Se isso for de maior interesse", "podem tunelizar espontaneamente"). None of these would teach a learner anything false.

examples.source: and some of them are dedicated, on-premises systems that support partners in the IBM Quantum® Network
examples.suggested: e alguns deles são sistemas dedicados instalados nas dependências do cliente (on-premises) que apoiam parceiros na IBM Quantum® Network
examples.translation: e alguns deles são sistemas dedicados em premissas que apoiam parceiros na IBM Quantum® Network
examples.why: "em premissas" is a false-friend calque of "on-premises"; in Portuguese "premissa" means a logical premise, so the phrase reads as nonsense. Native usage keeps "on-premises" or says "nas dependências do cliente" / "locais".

examples.source: translate the outcomes for your problem that you want to measure or understand into an expectation value or a cost function
examples.suggested: traduza ... em um valor esperado ou função de custo
examples.translation: traduza os resultados para o seu problema que você deseja medir ou entender em um valor de expectativa ou função de custo
examples.why: The conventional Portuguese physics/quantum term for "expectation value" is "valor esperado" (or "valor de expectação"); "valor de expectativa" is a literal calque. Recognizable and used consistently (also lines 147 and 159), so it is a MINOR terminology slip rather than a false concept.

examples.source: The two primitives that are most important to us are Sampler and Estimator … There are two primitives to choose from: Sampler and Estimator.
examples.suggested: Use the capitalized product names "o Sampler e o Estimator" in both places.
examples.translation: As duas primitivas mais importantes para nós são o sampler e o estimator … Há duas primitivas para escolher: o Sampler e o Estimator.
examples.why: Within-file inconsistency in how the two Qiskit Runtime primitive names are cased; the first occurrence lowercases them as if they were common nouns, the second treats them as the API class names. The concept stays identifiable, so this is minor, but an editor would unify it.

examples.source: Next, we'll need to choose a quantum processor that has enough qubits of high enough quality that we can run our quantum circuit.
examples.suggested: Em seguida, precisamos escolher um processador quântico com qubits em quantidade e qualidade suficientes para executar nosso circuito quântico.
examples.translation: Em seguida, precisamos escolher um processador quântico que tenha qubits suficientes de qualidade alta o suficiente para podermos executar nosso circuito quântico.
examples.why: The doubled "suficientes … o suficiente" is an awkward mirror of the English "enough … enough" that a Portuguese technical writer would collapse into a single construction; grammatical but audibly translated.

editor_note: Faithful and idiomatic throughout: the intro keeps the exact contrast ("versão de desenvolvimento atual, em vez de usar a versão no repositório Python Package Index (PyPI)"), the editable-mode caveat survives intact ("Modo editável: ... você não precisa reinstalar o Qiskit quando houver alterações de código no projeto" plus "as extensões compiladas são construídas em _modo de depuração_ sem otimizações"), and the "(Opcional)" qualifier on step 4 is preserved; register is consistently informal "você" (Navegue, Ative, Clone, Instale).

Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no hallucination; the delicate passages (the "fun" = minimum value not last value explanation, success=False meaning no convergence, the error-mitigation/gradient-washout paragraph, "apenas uma fila inicial antes do início do job") all match the English, and terminology is correct and consistent (Hamiltoniano, ansatz, otimizador clássico, valor esperado, portas swap, backend, gerenciador de passes; informal "você" holds). Two things a native editor would fix: (1) the third bullet in the session/options list is DUPLICATED — line 266 is the untranslated English "Estimator's built-in resilience: As with optimization…" bullet left in place, immediately followed at line 267 by its Portuguese rendering "Resiliência integrada do Estimator: …", so the reader sees the same item twice, once in English; (2) line 147 has the non-word verb "os qubits se decoerênciam com o tempo" — Portuguese has no verb "decoerênciar"; a native writer would write "os qubits sofrem decoerência ao longo do tempo". Neither misleads about the physics, hence MINOR rather than FAIL.

examples.source: Estimator's built-in resilience: As with optimization, Estimator has built-in settings for resilience against errors, corresponding to different approaches to error mitigation.
examples.suggested: Delete the leftover English bullet at line 266 and keep only the Portuguese bullet at line 267.
examples.translation:
* Estimator's built-in resilience: As with optimization, Estimator has built-in settings for resilience against errors… (line 266, untranslated English)
* Resiliência integrada do Estimator: assim como a otimização, o Estimator tem configurações integradas de resiliência contra erros… (line 267)
examples.why: A merge/splice artifact left the source-language bullet in the file alongside its translation, so the same list item appears twice and one of the two is in English. Not semantically misleading, but a visible defect a Portuguese reader would immediately notice.

examples.source: Since multi-qubit gates have high error rates and qubits decohere over time, the shorter circuits should give better results.
examples.suggested: Como as portas de múltiplos qubits têm altas taxas de erro e os qubits sofrem decoerência ao longo do tempo, circuitos mais curtos devem dar melhores resultados.
examples.translation: Como as portas de múltiplos qubits têm altas taxas de erro e os qubits se decoerênciam com o tempo, circuitos mais curtos devem dar melhores resultados.
examples.why: "se decoerênciam" is not a Portuguese verb — it is an invented back-formation from the noun "decoerência". The standard technical phrasing is "sofrem decoerência" (or "decoerem"). The concept is still recoverable, so it is a fluency slip, not a false concept.

examples.source: Execute using Qiskit Primitives / the Qiskit primitive, Estimator
examples.suggested: as primitivas do Qiskit / a primitiva do Qiskit, o Estimator
examples.translation: Executar usando os Primitivos do Qiskit / o primitivo do Qiskit, o Estimator
examples.why: Portuguese quantum-computing material generally uses the feminine "primitiva(s)" for Qiskit primitives (matching "primitives" as a class of routines). "Primitivo" reads as the adjective "primitive/early". It is used consistently in this file and remains recognizable, so this is a defensible-but-imperfect choice rather than a real error.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: the physics is transferred faithfully (ε₀ → "limita de stres proporțional", σ₀ → "limita de deformare proporțională", u/σ as stress/strain functions all match the English exactly, including the English's own odd symbol assignment), the grids (t, x între 0 și 0.95, pas 0.2375; x între 0 și 1, pas 0.04) and the benchmark table are intact, and the informal "tu" register holds throughout ("poți", "încearcă", "Consultă"). Three editorial slips: (1) mechanics terminology uses the English calque "stres" ("limita de stres proporțional", "funcția de stres", "stresul de suprafață") where Romanian technical writing says "tensiune"/"efort unitar" — recognizable but not the conventional domain term; (2) "is packaged as a Qiskit Function" is rendered "este ambalat ca o Funcție Qiskit", where "ambalat" is the physical-wrapping sense, not the software sense ("împachetat"/"livrat"); (3) a sentence-ending period is dropped after the arXiv link, welding two sentences together ("...a ColibriTD](...) Acest algoritm poate rezolva..."), and "the default [optimization sequence]" is pluralized into "valorile implicite" ("the default values"), shifting the referent from the sequence to its parameters.

examples.source: $\epsilon_0$ the proportional stress limit ... $u$ the stress function ... a boundary condition for surface stress $t$
examples.suggested: limita de tensiune proporțională ... funcția de tensiune ... condiție la limită pentru tensiunea superficială $t$
examples.translation: $\epsilon_0$ limita de stres proporțional ... $u$ funcția de stres ... o condiție la limită pentru stresul de suprafață $t$
examples.why: In Romanian continuum-mechanics writing, mechanical stress is "tensiune" (or "efort unitar"); "stres" is the psychological/colloquial borrowing. Meaning is still recoverable from context and the paired "deformare" (strain), so this is a naturalness/convention slip, not a false concept — but a native technical editor would change every occurrence.

editor_note: The translation collapses the two distinct transpiler concepts "stage" and "pass" into the single word "etapă", which destroys the structural point the whole of section 3 teaches. "Fluxul este compus din șase etape" (six stages: init/layout/routing/...) sits next to "să desenăm toate sarcinile (etapele transpiler-ului) din etapa `init`" — i.e. "the transpiler's stages inside the init stage" — and section 4.1 states "Pentru nivelurile 2 și 3, avem mai multe etape (`Collect2qBlocks`, `ConsolidateBlocks`, `UnitarySynthesis`)", which asserts something false: optimization levels 2 and 3 have the SAME six stages, only more passes inside the optimization stage. "pass" needs its own rendering ("pas"/"pass" — note "pași" is already used correctly for "steps" in 4.1: "compusă din doi pași"). Secondary: in 3.4 the hedge in "is used to try and minimize the size and depth" is dropped ("este utilizată pentru a reduce..."), turning a best-effort into a guarantee, and the Admonition has an ungrammatical genitive, "Descarcă PDF-ul al cursului original".

The learner forms a false belief about what optimization_level changes.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: the physics is faithful end-to-end (little-endian ordering, CNOT flipping the target only if the control is |1⟩, the 50/50 outcomes, the "superposition is not literally both states at once" caveat, the glued-coins analogy) and the informal "tu" register holds throughout with no dumneavoastră/vă slips. What a native technical editor would still change is a cluster of calques and one wrong-gender term: "de-a lungul unui singur ax" uses the masculine "ax" (shaft/axle) where Romanian geometry requires "axă" — and the same file later gets it right with "de-a lungul a trei axe diferite"; "Poți gândi starea |0⟩ ca un vector" is a raw calque of "you can think of X as Y" (Romanian needs "Te poți gândi la ... ca la un vector"), and line 165 half-corrects it to "Poți gândi mai intuitiv la aceasta"; "garantăm că obținem un rezultat" turns the English passive "we are guaranteed to get some outcome" into an active claim that we do the guaranteeing. Smaller items: "va rezulta într-un vector de stare" and "de ce este cazul" are anglicisms, "eigenstările lor" (calque) sits next to "termenul eigenstate" in the same paragraph where Romanian convention is "stări proprii", "jgheabul celuilalt" renders a wave trough with the word for a gutter/feeding-trough instead of "valea/golul undei", "bus de informații clasice" would normally be "magistrală", and the qualifier "alone" is dropped from "impossible with classical randomness alone".

examples.why: "ax" (masculine) is a mechanical shaft/axle; the geometric axis is "axă" (feminine). The same file uses the correct form later ("de-a lungul a trei axe diferite"), so it is also an internal inconsistency.

examples.source: You can think of the |0⟩ state as a vector pointing straight up

examples.why: The English passive (we are guaranteed) becomes an active claim that we are the ones doing the guaranteeing — grammatical but stiff and slightly off in sense; the underlying point (some outcome always occurs) survives, so this is a naturalness slip, not drift.

examples.why: "jgheab" is a gutter or feeding-trough, not the trough of a wave; Romanian physics uses "valea" (or "golul") undei. The wave analogy is still recoverable but the image is briefly broken.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — every number, date and revision claim matches (120/156/133 qubiți, decembrie 2025, iulie 2024, "actualizare de dimensiunea Eagle a lui Egret", "implementate anterior în Osprey"), no inverted conditions, no hallucinated sentences, and the informal "tu" register holds consistently (folosește / Poți vedea / Consultă / Vezi). Three editorial slips remain. (1) The tip admonition drifts from the current English: title "Supported instruction set" and body "the supported instruction set for a backend … all supported instructions" are rendered as the narrower, older wording "Gate-uri și operații native" / "gate-urile și operațiile native ale unui Backend" — it still points at the right section so it does not mislead, but it no longer says what the source says. (2) "heavy-hexagonal lattice" is calqued as "rețea hexagonală grea", where "grea" reads as physically heavy rather than the heavy-hex topology name. (3) "signal delivery" is rendered word-for-word as "livrare de semnal" (twice), which a Romanian hardware writer would phrase as "transmiterea/distribuția semnalului".

examples.source: <Admonition type="tip" title="Supported instruction set"> To find the supported instruction set for a backend, use [this code]. You can see all supported instructions in [this table].

examples.why: The translation carries the page's older wording ("native gates and operations") instead of the current source's broader "supported instruction set", which also covers non-gate instructions such as measure/delay/reset. It still resolves to the correct linked section, so it is not misleading, but it is a divergence from the English the reader is nominally reading.

examples.source: The chip has been redesigned to include 156 qubits in a heavy-hexagonal lattice.

examples.translation: Cipul a fost reproiectat pentru a include 156 de qubiți într-o rețea hexagonală grea.
examples.why: "Grea" is the weight sense of "heavy"; the IBM lattice name refers to the heavy-hex graph topology, not to anything being heavy. Recognizable in context, but it is a literal calque of a named topology and a Romanian hardware writer would keep "heavy-hex" or gloss it.

examples.translation: … stiva noastră tehnologică de la Heron (cuploare, livrare de semnal și coerență) …; … inovații substanțiale în livrarea de semnal …
examples.why: "Livrare de semnal" is a word-for-word calque of "signal delivery"; "livrare" in Romanian is delivery of goods. Native microwave/hardware usage is "transmiterea" or "distribuția semnalului". Stiff rather than wrong.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: every tab (City, Hinton, Pauli vector, QSphere, Bloch) matches its English paragraph, including the caveats "Nu poate arăta corelațiile dintre Qubiți... nu poate descrie complet stările cuantice entanglate" and "Este posibil să vizualizezi doar stările sistemelor cuantice mici". What a native editor would still change: (1) the frontmatter/sidebar title reframes the page from "Plot quantum states" to "Vizualizări de informații cuantice" ("quantum information"), which is not what the page is about; (2) "rich objects" becomes "obiecte complexe", which in a quantum text invites confusion with complex numbers — "obiecte bogate/structurate" is meant; (3) "expected value / expectation value" is split into "valoarea așteptată" then "valoarea de așteptare" in the same sentence, the latter being a calque (native usage: "valoarea medie" / "valoarea așteptată"), and only "valoare de așteptare" is used thereafter; (4) a plain typo, "este cunoscuta" for "este cunoscută"; (5) the quantifier in "Tensor products of Pauli matrices are all observables that return +1 or -1" loses its "all" ("sunt observabile care returnează"). Register is correctly informal throughout ("Îți recomandăm", "Ai nevoie să îți reîmprospătezi").

examples.translation: Valoarea așteptată a rezultatului este cunoscuta și sub numele de valoarea de așteptare a observabilului pe acea stare

examples.translation: Produsele tensoriale ale matricelor Pauli sunt observabile care returnează +1 sau -1.
examples.why: The universal quantifier "all" is dropped, weakening the claim from "every such tensor product is a ±1 observable" to "some are" — the sentence is the premise for the Pauli decomposition that follows.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the three execution modes, the Open-plan restriction ("Utilizatorii planului Open nu pot trimite joburi de Session"), the batch conditional ("dacă toate joburile pot fi furnizate de la început"), the close-session rationale and the PUB note all match the English with no drift, no dropped caveat and nothing invented; register is consistently informal ("Poți rula", "Consultă", "Află cum să transpilezi local"). The two defects are word-order calques around the word "primitive". In the lead paragraph "sarcinile de lucru Qiskit primitive" puts "primitive" in Romanian adjective position, so it parses as "primitive/rudimentary Qiskit workloads" instead of "workloads that use Qiskit primitives" (should be "sarcinile de lucru cu primitive Qiskit"). In the job-mode section "o singură cerere primitivă către Estimator sau Sampler" has the same problem — "cerere primitivă" reads as "crude request" rather than "a request to a primitive" ("o singură cerere de primitivă Estimator sau Sampler"). Neither teaches a false quantum concept, so both are minor; note also the mild Session/sesiune alternation ("Odată ce o Session este configurată... trimise în aceeași sesiune"), which mirrors the English and is defensible.

examples.source: You can run your Qiskit primitive workloads using REST APIs in one of three execution modes, depending on your needs: job, session, and batch.
examples.suggested: Poți rula sarcinile de lucru cu primitive Qiskit folosind REST API în unul din trei moduri de execuție, în funcție de nevoile tale: job, session și batch.

examples.why: In Romanian the postposed 'primitive' is read as an adjective qualifying 'sarcinile de lucru', so the phrase says 'primitive/rudimentary Qiskit workloads' rather than 'workloads built on Qiskit primitives'. The noun reading ('cu primitive Qiskit') is needed to preserve the domain term.

Also the passive 'este efectuată' is a stiff calque where a reflexive ('se trimite') is the natural Romanian technical construction.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no hallucination. I checked the risk points paragraph by paragraph: the TTL section keeps the exact split ("Anumang mga job na tumatakbo ay matatapos, ngunit ang mga job na nasa queue pa ay mabibigo"), the 1-minute non-configurable interactive TTL, the 8 oras / 10 minuto table, "ayon sa pagkakasunod" for "respectively", the close-batch tip (subsequent jobs canceled if max TTL is hit; already-submitted jobs still run to completion and results retrievable), and the caution that `backend=backend` forces job mode even inside a batch/session and is deprecated as of v0.24.0. Two cosmetic things a native editor would fix: the misspelling "naisumiiteng" (doubled i; should be "naisumiteng") in the close-batch Admonition, and the stacked-linker, number-mismatched heading "Default na maximum na TTL values:" (double "na" plus English plural on a Tagalog phrase). Neither misleads.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no drift, no hallucination, no inverted conditions; the two load-bearing technical claims survive intact ("nasa itaas ng break-even point" for "above the break-even point", "nasa ibaba ng isang tiyak na threshold" for "below a certain threshold"), and the logical/physical qubit distinction and the "hindi kailanman nalantad" (never exposed) caveat are all correct. What a native technical editor would change is wording, not content: "naitatayo ang entropy" uses the verb for erecting a structure where entropy *accumulates* ("naiipon" is the idiomatic choice), "simpleng nag-iingat lang sila ng quantum information" says the qubits *safeguard* rather than *store* information ("nag-iimbak"), and "Ang anumang klasikal na computation na kabilang" is a stiff calque of "that are involved". There is also a first-person pronoun break in "mayroon kaming pundamental na tanong na maaari naming itanong sa ating sarili", which switches to exclusive kami/naming inside a sentence that ends in inclusive "ating" — the rest of the file uses tayo/natin consistently. Informal register otherwise holds; no po/opo.

examples.source: As errors take place, entropy builds up, and constant work is required to remove it from the system at a high enough rate
examples.suggested: Habang nagaganap ang mga error, naiipon ang entropy, at kinakailangan ang patuloy na trabaho para alisin ito mula sa system nang sapat na bilis
examples.translation: Habang nagaganap ang mga error, naitatayo ang entropy, at kinakailangan ang patuloy na trabaho para alisin ito mula sa system nang sapat na bilis
examples.why: "naitatayo" is the verb for erecting/constructing something physical; entropy accumulates. "naiipon" (or "nag-iipon") is what a Tagalog technical writer would use for "builds up". Not misleading, but audibly non-native.
