examples.why: "na kabilang" is a bare calque of "that are involved" and dangles without a complement; "kasangkot" (or "na ginagamit dito") is the natural rendering.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the load-bearing caveat in "Add and update tags" survives intact ("Pina-overwrite ng pamamaraang ito ang mga kasalukuyang tag ... siguraduhing i-re-assign din ang mga orihinal na tag"), the "isa o maraming tag" quantity and the "sa paglaon" (later) filtering condition both match the English, and register is correctly informal (puwede/iyong, no po/opo). Two things a native technical editor would still change: "method" is rendered two different ways in consecutive sentences of the same paragraph — "gamit ang `update_tags()` na paraan" then "Pina-overwrite ng pamamaraang ito" — where one consistent rendering (or simply keeping "method", which is the usual convention for an API method) is wanted; and line 32 writes "ma-subaybayan" with a hyphen, which Tagalog orthography reserves for foreign/English roots — "subaybay" is a native root, so it should be "masubaybayan". Neither could mislead a learner about job tags.

examples.source: You can add tags after you submit a job with the `update_tags()` method. This method overwrites current tags, ...
examples.suggested: ... gamit ang `update_tags()` method. Ino-overwrite ng method na ito ang mga kasalukuyang tag, ...
examples.translation: Puwede kang magdagdag ng mga tag pagkatapos mag-submit ng job gamit ang `update_tags()` na paraan. Pina-overwrite ng pamamaraang ito ang mga kasalukuyang tag, ...
examples.why: The same term "method" is rendered as "paraan" and then "pamamaraan" in back-to-back sentences; for an API method name the field normally keeps "method" in English, and in any case one rendering should be used consistently within the paragraph.

examples.source: ... so that you can better organize, track, and understand your experiments.
examples.suggested: ... para mas maayos mong ma-organisa, masubaybayan, at maunawaan ang iyong mga eksperimento.
examples.translation: ... para mas maayos mong ma-organisa, ma-subaybayan, at maunawaan ang iyong mga eksperimento.
examples.why: The hyphen in "ma-subaybayan" is incorrect: Tagalog hyphenates affixes only before foreign/English roots (ma-organisa is fine), while "subaybay" is a native root and takes the affix directly. A native technical writer would write "masubaybayan".

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the comparative "mas pangkalahatang klase ng measurements … kaysa sa mga tinalakay sa Basics of quantum information" preserves the EN comparison, and the Credly paragraph keeps every element (third-party processor, IBM-authorized, US-located, exact shared-data list). Three things a native technical editor would still change: (1) line 20 uses perfective "inilarawan" where the general present "inilalarawan" is needed, clashing with the correctly imperfective "kinakatawan" in the same sentence; (2) line 40 "para tulungan sa pamamahala" is a calque of "to assist in the administration" — "tulungan" is transitive with no object here, so "para tumulong sa pamamahala" is the natural form; (3) line 30 hardens "is intended to be taken" into an obligation with "dapat gawin". Minor consistency wrinkle: "## Exam" is translated to "## Eksamen" but "## Awarded Badge" is left in English. Informal register holds — no po/opo anywhere.

examples.source: changes in states are described by *channels,*
examples.suggested: ang mga pagbabago sa state ay inilalarawan ng *channels,*
examples.translation: ang mga pagbabago sa state ay inilarawan ng *channels,*
examples.why: Perfective 'inilarawan' reads as a completed past action; the English is a general present and the coordinated verb in the same sentence ('kinakatawan') is correctly imperfective, so the aspect mismatch is audible within one sentence.

examples.source: to assist in the administration of the IBM Digital Badge program
examples.suggested: para tumulong sa pamamahala ng IBM Digital Badge program
examples.translation: para tulungan sa pamamahala ng IBM Digital Badge program
examples.why: Calqued English syntax: 'tulungan' is a transitive (object-focus) form left without an object, which a Tagalog writer would not produce. The actor-focus 'tumulong sa' is the idiomatic rendering of 'assist in'.

examples.source: This exam is intended to be taken after reading the lessons in this course.
examples.suggested: Ang eksamen na ito ay nilalayong kunin pagkatapos basahin ang mga aralin sa kursong ito.
examples.translation: Ang eksamen na ito ay dapat gawin pagkatapos basahin ang mga aralin sa kursong ito.
examples.why: 'dapat' turns IBM's recommendation ('is intended to be taken') into an obligation. Mild strengthening of the claim, not misleading about any technical content, but it changes the source's modality.

examples.source: ## Awarded Badge
examples.suggested: ## Iginawad na Badge
examples.translation: ## Awarded Badge
examples.why: Within-file inconsistency in heading policy: '## Exam' was translated to '## Eksamen' but this sibling heading was left entirely in English. Noted as inconsistency only — kept-term/leak handling is out of scope for this run.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: the resilience caveat ("Hindi sinusuportahan ng Sampler V2 ang pagtukoy ng mga antas ng resilience"), the PUB definition ("isang tuple na naglalaman ng isang circuit at ng data na ina-broadcast sa circuit na iyon ... nagbabalik ng isang resulta bawat PUB"), the Open Plan restriction, and the deliberate section-1 vs parameterized-section-1 split between "gumana gamit ang mga token" and "i-invalidate ang mga token" all track the English; register is informal with no po/opo. The recurring editorial defect is the calque "gumana gamit ang" for English "work with", used three times (H5 heading "Gumana gamit ang mga opsyon ng Qiskit Runtime", "at gumana gamit ang mga token", "Matuto kung paano gumana gamit ang session mode at batch mode") — "gumana" is intransitive "to function/operate" in Tagalog, so the phrase reads as "to function by means of X"; a native technical writer would write "Paggamit ng ..." or "magtrabaho gamit ang ...". Two smaller stiffness points: "Python na module na `requests`" is an English noun-order calque (natural: "module ng Python na `requests`"), and "ilunsad" (= launch) is used for "invoke them in any program of your choice" where "tawagin/gamitin" is the conventional rendering. None of these would mislead a learner.

examples.source: Work with Qiskit Runtime options / work with tokens / Learn how to work with session mode and batch mode
examples.suggested: Paggamit ng mga opsyon ng Qiskit Runtime / magtrabaho gamit ang mga token / Matuto kung paano gamitin ang session mode at batch mode
examples.translation: Gumana gamit ang mga opsyon ng Qiskit Runtime / gumana gamit ang mga token / Matuto kung paano gumana gamit ang session mode at batch mode
examples.why: "Gumana" is intransitive in Tagalog (a machine gumagana); "gumana gamit ang X" literally says "to function by means of X", a direct calque of English "work with". Occurs three times, so it also sets a stiff pattern for the reader.

examples.source: This documentation utilizes the Python `requests` module
examples.suggested: Ang dokumentasyong ito ay gumagamit ng `requests` module ng Python
examples.translation: Ang dokumentasyong ito ay gumagamit ng Python na module na `requests`
examples.why: English attributive noun order carried straight into Tagalog; the double linker "Python na module na" is something no native technical writer would produce.

examples.source: demonstrate how to invoke them in any program of your choice
examples.suggested: nagpapakita kung paano tawagin/gamitin ang mga ito sa anumang programa na gusto mo
examples.translation: nagpapakita kung paano ilunsad ang mga ito sa anumang programa ng iyong pagpili
examples.why: "Ilunsad" means "to launch" (an event, a product), not "to invoke" an API call; recognizable in context so not misleading, but the conventional rendering is "tawagin" or "gamitin".

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the superposition/2^n coin argument, the measurement-collapse caveat ("isa lamang ang maaring makuha nating resulta"), the scarf entanglement analogy including its "hindi perpekto" caveat, and all six key takeaways (incl. "mas mahina kaysa sa exponential parallelism") all land correctly, and register stays casual with no po/opo. What a native technical editor would still change: (1) in the quiz option (b), "strongly correlated" is rendered "mahalagang magkaugnay" ("importantly correlated") — the strength qualifier is replaced by a relevance one; (2) "which we will denote $x_i$" becomes "na ididiin natin" ("which we will emphasize/press"), the wrong verb for "denote"; (3) the musical-chord passage uses actor-focus "tumutugtog" where English is passive ("a chord ... is played on a guitar", "a violin is played more loudly") — should be "tinutugtog"/"tinugtog"; (4) "all information is reducible to bits" is calqued as "maaaring bawasan sa mga bit" (bawasan = diminish in quantity, not express-as); (5) "dispels several myths" → "Winawakasan ... ang ilang mga mito" reads as "terminates the myths" rather than "pinapabulaanan"; (6) small typos/slips: "maaring" (for maaaring), "paguusap", "pagtutugog", and "kakayahang mag-imbak at manipulahin ng impormasyon" (focus/marker mismatch). None of these would make a learner form a false belief about quantum computing.

examples.source: Two systems that are too far apart to influence each other are somehow strongly correlated.
examples.suggested: ... ay kahit papaano ay malakas na magkaugnay.
examples.translation: Ang dalawang sistema na masyadong malayo upang makaapekto sa isa't isa ay kahit papaano ay mahalagang magkaugnay.
examples.why: "mahalaga" = important/significant-in-value, not "strong". The quiz item is about the STRENGTH of the correlation between spacelike-separated systems; rendering it as "importantly correlated" swaps the qualifier and blunts the counterintuitive point.

examples.source: This process depends on many input variables, which we will denote $x_i$.
examples.suggested: ... na tutukuyin natin bilang $x_i$.
examples.translation: Ang prosesong ito ay nakasalalay sa maraming mga input variable, na ididiin natin bilang $x_i$.
examples.why: "ididiin" means "will emphasize / press down on"; "denote" here is notational naming. "tutukuyin" / "isusulat natin bilang" is the conventional technical rendering.

examples.source: when a chord of several musical notes is played on a guitar … when a violin is played more loudly than the other instruments
examples.suggested: kapag tinutugtog sa gitara ang isang chord ng ilang nota … kapag mas malakas na tinutugtog ang violin
examples.translation: kapag isang chord ng ilang musikal na nota ay tumutugtog sa isang gitara … kapag ang isang violin ay tumutugtog nang mas malakas
examples.why: "tumutugtog" is actor-focus (the chord/violin is the one doing the playing); the English is passive. A native writer would use "tinutugtog". Same slip at "ang isa sa mga nota na tumutugtog" (should be "na tinugtog").

examples.source: In this model, all information is reducible to bits …
examples.suggested: … lahat ng impormasyon ay maaaring ipahayag bilang mga bit …
examples.translation: Sa modelong ito, lahat ng impormasyon ay maaaring bawasan sa mga bit …
examples.why: "bawasan" means to reduce in amount/quantity, not to reduce-to in the representational sense. A calque that reads oddly to a Tagalog technical reader, though context keeps the meaning recoverable.

examples.source: Katie Pizzolato … dispels several quantum computing myths in 60 seconds.
examples.suggested: Pinapabulaanan ni Katie Pizzolato … ang ilang mito …
examples.translation: Winawakasan ni Katie Pizzolato … ang ilang mga mito tungkol sa quantum computing sa loob ng 60 segundo.
examples.why: "Winawakasan" = brings to an end/terminates; "dispel a myth" is "pumabulaan/magpawalang-bisa". Defensible in the loosest reading but not what a native technical writer would pick.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the `Unset`/server-default explanation, the "primitive makes a copy so changing the original doesn't affect it" caveat, and the auto-complete vs `update()` bulk-update contrast all survive intact, and the register stays informal (mo/iyong, no po/opo). What a native editor would change is word choice: "constructed" is rendered as "itayo"/"magtayo" (lines 29, 31), which in Tagalog means to erect a building or establish an organization — a technical writer would write "bago gawin/buuin ang primitive" or "bago ma-instantiate". "method" is over-translated to "paraan" ("built-in na paraan na `asdict`" line 36, "paraan na `update()`" line 98) where the field keeps "method". "initialization" is split within the file between "pagsisimula" (lines 34, 96, 100) and "nagsi-initialize" (line 71); both are recognizable, so the concept is never lost. Line 41 "ilalapat pagkatapos kapag ginamit mo ang `run()`" is redundantly stiff ("then...when" calqued literally). None of these mislead.

examples.source: Options can be defined before a primitive is constructed and passed to the primitive ... Additionally, you can change the options after the primitive is constructed.
examples.suggested: ... bago buuin/gawin ang isang primitive ... pagkatapos gawin ang primitive (or: pagkatapos ma-instantiate ang primitive)
examples.translation: Maaaring tukuyin ang mga opsyon bago pa itayo ang isang primitive ... Bukod pa rito, maaari mong baguhin ang mga opsyon pagkatapos magtayo ng primitive.
examples.why: 'Itayo/magtayo' means to erect a structure or found an institution; applied to a Python object it reads as a literal dictionary pick, not how a Tagalog-speaking engineer would describe object construction. Meaning still recovers from context, so it does not mislead.

examples.source: You can use the built-in `asdict` method ... or use the `update()` method to make bulk updates.
examples.suggested: ... ang built-in na `asdict` method ... o gamitin ang `update()` method ...
examples.translation: Maaari mong gamitin ang built-in na paraan na `asdict` ... o gamitin ang paraan na `update()` para sa maramihang pag-update.
examples.why: 'Paraan' is a generic word for 'way/manner'; 'method' as an OOP term is normally kept in English in Tagalog technical prose. It is consistent within the file and still recognizable, so it is an over-translation rather than a false concept.

examples.source: when initializing a primitive / after initializing the primitive
examples.suggested: Pick one: use 'pag-initialize' (or 'pagsisimula') consistently for all three occurrences.
examples.translation: kapag nagsi-initialize ng primitive (l.71) vs. pagkatapos ng pagsisimula ng primitive (l.96, l.100)
examples.why: The same concept is rendered two different ways within one short file; a learner may briefly wonder whether 'pagsisimula' means something other than initialization, though both are recoverable so the concept stays identifiable.

editor_note: Nothing in this file misleads: the two protocols are transferred accurately — the teleportation correction table keeps the source's "01"→X / "10"→Z pairing, the little-endian q2=|0⟩ conclusion, the no-cloning answer ("nawala ang orihinal na quantum state ... sa pagsukat"), and the superdense-coding contrast ("Sa teleportation, available ang klasikal na komunikasyon ... Dito, hindi available") are all faithful, and domain terms (qubit, gate, e-bit, computational basis, coupling map, transpile→"pag-transpile") are consistent. What a native technical editor would still change: (1) "complex numbers" is rendered as "mga kumplikadong numero" (§1) — a false friend reading as "complicated numbers" — while §3 keeps "complex number" in English, so the same term is split two ways; (2) "utility-scale work" becomes "kababalaghang utility-scale" ("utility-scale phenomenon/wonder"), and "fairly/reasonably accurate" is twice rendered "makatotohanang tumpak" ("realistically accurate"); (3) two small flattenings — "we will *sometimes* use language..." loses "sometimes", and "generating such a state is where we will begin this lesson" collapses to a referent-less "dito tayo magsisimula ng araling ito"; (4) calques/grammar slips: "matagumpay na nagtrabaho ang teleportation protocol" (should be "gumana"), "matuto nang ukol sa" (×2), "kung kailangan mong magpaalala", and one exclusive-"aming" slip in a file that is otherwise consistently inclusive "natin". Register is correctly casual throughout — no po/opo.

examples.source: where $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are complex numbers such that $|\alpha|^2+|\beta|^2 = 1$
examples.suggested: kung saan ang $\alpha$ at $\beta$ ay mga complex number na nagtutugon sa ...
examples.translation: kung saan ang $\alpha$ at $\beta$ ay mga kumplikadong numero na nagtutugon sa $|\alpha|^2+|\beta|^2 = 1$
examples.why: "Kumplikado" means "complicated", not the mathematical "complex" — a classic false friend. The file itself keeps "complex number" in English in §3 ("ang impormasyon ng complex number"), so the same term is rendered two ways within the file.

examples.source: But by its very nature, utility-scale work is not always so trivial to check.
examples.suggested: Ngunit dahil sa likas nitong katangian, ang gawaing utility-scale ay hindi laging ganoon kadali suriin.
examples.translation: Ngunit sa likas ng kababalaghang utility-scale, hindi laging ganoon kadali suriin ang mga resulta.
examples.why: "Kababalaghan" means a marvel/strange phenomenon; "utility-scale work" is "gawain", not a wonder. Also "sa likas ng" is an incomplete idiom (needs "sa likas na katangian ng"). Reads as machine output at a point where the English is plain.

examples.source: Since we want to be able to transfer the information in any random quantum state, generating such a state is where we will begin this lesson.
examples.suggested: Dahil gusto nating maipadala ang impormasyon sa anumang random na quantum state, ang paglikha ng gayong state ang pagsisimulan natin sa araling ito.
examples.translation: Dahil gusto nating makapagpadala ng impormasyon sa anumang random na quantum state, dito tayo magsisimula ng araling ito.
examples.why: The clause "generating such a state" is dropped, leaving "dito" with no antecedent. The sentence is the pedagogical hinge into §2 (creating a random state); the learner loses why the lesson starts there.

examples.source: This is the expected result, and indicates the teleportation protocol has worked properly.
examples.suggested: ... at nagpapakita na gumana nang maayos ang teleportation protocol.
examples.translation: Ito ang inaasahang resulta, at nagpapakita na matagumpay na nagtrabaho ang teleportation protocol.
examples.why: "Nagtrabaho" is a literal calque of "worked" in the sense of doing labor; Tagalog uses "gumana" for a mechanism/protocol functioning. No native technical writer would say a protocol "nagtrabaho".

examples.source: The result is what we expected.
examples.suggested: Ang resulta ay ayon sa inaasahan natin.
examples.translation: Ang resulta ay ayon sa aming inaasahan.
examples.why: The file consistently uses inclusive "natin/nating" for the teaching voice ("natantiya natin", "isasagawa natin", "Matututunan natin"); the exclusive "aming" here suddenly excludes the reader from the shared expectation.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: every claim (v0.27.1 / v0.47.0 version gating, "NoiseLearner only works with EstimatorV2 and NoiseLearnerV3 only works with Executor", the three-boxes / two-with-InjectNoise example, the ref→noise-map dictionary explanation) matches the English exactly, and the informal register holds throughout. The defects are grammatical/naturalness only. Twice the passive "learned" is rendered with the actor-focus verb "natuto" — "noise model na natuto para sa ibinigay na layer" (~L91) and "Ang noise model na natuto sa circuit" (~L205) literally say "the noise model that learned", where a native writer would write "natutunan". "groups instructions into annotated boxes" becomes "nagpogroup ng mga instruction" (~L341), a malformed Taglish verb (should be "nagpapangkat" / "nag-gu-group"). Also "noise" is rendered as "ingay" in "mga proseso ng ingay" (~L45, ~L235, ~L339) while every other occurrence keeps "noise" (noise model, noise map, noise learning) — an in-file split — and "characterize" is flattened to "nagtatasa" (assess) rather than "naglalarawan/nagkakaraktersa".

examples.source: alongside the `PauliLindbladError` for the noise model that was learned for the given layer
examples.suggested: ... para sa noise model na natutunan para sa ibinigay na layer
examples.translation: kasama ang `PauliLindbladError` para sa noise model na natuto para sa ibinigay na layer
examples.why: "natuto" is actor-focus ("the model that learned"); the English is passive ("that was learned"). Correct form is "natutunan". Same slip recurs at ~L205 ("Ang noise model na natuto sa circuit").

examples.source: runs through the boxing pass manager, which groups instructions into annotated boxes
examples.suggested: ... na nagpapangkat ng mga instruction sa mga annotated box
examples.translation: tumatakbo sa pamamagitan ng boxing pass manager, na nagpogroup ng mga instruction sa mga annotated box
examples.why: "nagpogroup" is a malformed Taglish conjugation of "group" that no native technical writer would produce; "nagpapangkat" (or "nag-gu-group") is the natural form.

examples.source: performs experiments that characterize noise processes based on a Pauli-Lindblad noise model
examples.suggested: ... na naglalarawan ng mga proseso ng noise batay sa ...
examples.translation: nagsasagawa ng mga eksperimento na nagtatasa ng mga proseso ng ingay batay sa isang Pauli-Lindblad noise model
examples.why: Two small slips in one clause: "noise" is translated to "ingay" here (and ~L235, ~L339) but kept as English "noise" everywhere else in the file (noise model, noise map, noise learning), and "characterize" is weakened to "nagtatasa" (assess/appraise) rather than describe/characterize.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: every claim in the source survives intact, including the delicate negation pair "walang nagsasabing kailangan ni Bob na sukatin ... ngunit walang nagsasabing hindi rin niya ito gagawin", the "hindi lamang isang pure state" generalization, and the closing partial-trace worked examples. What a native technical editor would change is a cluster of false-friend calques: "complex numbers" → "mga kumplikadong numero" (reads as "complicated numbers"; the standard rendering is "kompleks na bilang" or the kept-English "complex numbers"), "placed in correspondence with" → "inilalagay sa pagsusulatan sa" (pagsusulatan = exchanging letters; the same idea is correctly rendered "tumutugma sa" two sections later, so the file is internally inconsistent), "independence" → "*kalayaan*" (political/personal freedom rather than statistical independence), and "satisfy the formulas" → "nagbibigay-kasiyahan sa mga formula". There is also one broken MT fragment, "Pagtutulad ng nang sa nakaraang halimbawa ng e-bit" (stray "ng nang", ungrammatical), plus "mas tumpak naming sinasabi" using exclusive kami-form in a document that is otherwise consistently inclusive natin/tayo, and "ang tanging paglalarawang pare-pareho sa imposibilidad ng komunikasyong mas mabilis kaysa sa liwanag" where "consistent with" should be "naaayon sa", not "pare-pareho". None of these would make a learner form a false belief, so this stays MINOR.

examples.source: for some choice of complex numbers $\{\alpha_{jk} : 0\leq j,k\leq 3\}.$
examples.suggested: para sa ilang pagpipilian ng mga complex number na $\{\alpha_{jk} : ...\}$
examples.translation: para sa ilang pagpipilian ng mga kumplikadong numero na $\{\alpha_{jk} : 0\leq j,k\leq 3\}.$
examples.why: "kumplikado" reads as "complicated", not the mathematical field C. The entries being complex (not merely messy) is the actual content of the sentence; Filipino technical writing keeps "complex number" or uses "kompleks na bilang".

examples.source: the rows and columns ... are placed in correspondence with the Cartesian product of the classical state sets
examples.suggested: ... ay itinutugma sa Cartesian product ng mga classical state set
examples.translation: ang mga hanay at kolum ... ay inilalagay sa pagsusulatan sa Cartesian product ng mga classical state set
examples.why: "pagsusulatan" is correspondence in the letter-writing sense, a false friend here. The file itself uses the right verb later ("tumutugma sa Cartesian product" at line 178, "tumutugma sa mga classical state" at line 311), so the rendering is also inconsistent within the file.

examples.source: Reasoning similarly to the previous example of an e-bit, if we were to measure the system $\mathsf{B}$ with a standard basis measurement,
examples.suggested: Sa katulad na pangangatwiran tulad ng sa nakaraang halimbawa ng e-bit, kung susukatin natin ang sistemang $\mathsf{B}$ gamit ang standard basis measurement,
examples.translation: Pagtutulad ng nang sa nakaraang halimbawa ng e-bit, kung susukat tayo ng sistema $\mathsf{B}$ gamit ang standard basis measurement,
examples.why: "Pagtutulad ng nang sa" is ungrammatical (stray "ng nang") and reads as raw MT; "susukat tayo ng sistema" also needs the goal focus "susukatin natin ang sistemang B".

examples.source: tensor products of density matrices represent *independence* between the states of multiple systems
examples.suggested: ... ay kumakatawan sa *pagsasarili* (independence) sa pagitan ng mga estado ng maramihang sistema
examples.translation: ang mga tensor product ng mga density matrix ay kumakatawan sa *kalayaan* sa pagitan ng mga estado ng maramihang sistema
examples.why: "kalayaan" is freedom/liberty (Araw ng Kalayaan), not statistical independence. Since this is the italicized defined term being introduced, the intended sense should not rest on the reader inferring it from the next sentence.

examples.source: to be more precise we say that the partial trace is performed on $\mathsf{B}$
examples.suggested: mas tumpak nating sinasabi na ang partial trace ay ginagawa sa $\mathsf{B}$
examples.translation: mas tumpak naming sinasabi na ang partial trace ay ginagawa sa $\mathsf{B}$
examples.why: "naming" is exclusive we (kami — excludes the reader); the whole lesson otherwise addresses the learner inclusively (natin/tayo: "maaari nating tukuyin", "nakuha natin"). One-word slip that breaks the teaching voice.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout this very short prose set — no drift, no inversion, no hallucination, and the informal "ти" convention holds consistently ("ти вже зберіг свої облікові дані", "дотримуйся інструкцій", "Ознайомся зі статтею"). Three editorial slips: (1) the product name Qiskit Functions is translated as "функції Qiskit" in the link "Введення у функції Qiskit", which contradicts the rest of the uk corpus (guides/functions.mdx is titled "Вступ до Qiskit Functions", and compute-services.mdx keeps "Qiskit Functions") and can read as ordinary Python functions rather than the IBM product; the link label also no longer matches the page it points to. (2) "quantum-centric supercomputing" (a computing paradigm) becomes "квантово-центричні суперкомп'ютери" — plural physical machines rather than the approach, flattening an IBM term of art. (3) minor style: "існуючий код" is a calque flagged by Ukrainian technical style guides (prefer "наявний код"), and "нотатки про випуск" for release notes is stiffer than the usual "примітки до випуску". None of these would teach a learner something false.

examples.source: Follow the instructions on the [Introduction to Qiskit Functions](/guides/functions) page to authenticate with your API key.
examples.suggested: Дотримуйся інструкцій на сторінці [Вступ до Qiskit Functions](/guides/functions) для автентифікації за допомогою API-ключа.
examples.translation: Дотримуйся інструкцій на сторінці [Введення у функції Qiskit](/guides/functions) для автентифікації за допомогою API-ключа.
examples.why: Qiskit Functions is a product name kept in English everywhere else in the uk corpus (functions.mdx title is "Вступ до Qiskit Functions"; compute-services.mdx keeps "Qiskit Functions"). Translating it to "функції Qiskit" both breaks that convention and makes the link label diverge from the target page's own title, and it can be misread as generic Python functions.

editor_note: This file is a pure bibliography: all 136 numbered entries are byte-identical English citations (titles, journals, DOIs, Wikipedia URLs), which is correct — bibliographic records should not be translated. The only translated prose is the frontmatter and the two headings, and it is faithful: "Works cited" → "Використані джерела", "Full list of references" → "Повний список посилань". The single editorial slip is in the description: "all citations used within the course" is rendered "список усіх цитат, використаних у курсі", where "цитата" in Ukrainian means a verbatim quotation, not a bibliographic citation; a native technical editor would write "список усіх джерел" (or "бібліографічних посилань"), which would also align with the page title "Використані джерела". Nothing here misleads a learner — no drift, no hallucination, no domain-term error; the informal-register question does not arise since there is no second-person prose.

examples.source: This document provides a list of all citations used within the course.

examples.translation: Цей документ містить список усіх цитат, використаних у курсі.
examples.why: "Цитата" is a verbatim quotation; a works-cited entry is a bibliographic reference ("джерело" / "посилання"). The page title already uses "Використані джерела", so "цитат" is both the less accurate term and inconsistent with the heading two lines below. Low severity — the reader still understands what the page contains.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — I found no semantic drift, inverted condition or hallucinated claim; the tricky passages (PEC/resilience-level-3 tradeoff, `Unset` + server defaults, V2→V1 counts/shots conversion, the (4,1)×(1,6)→(4,6) broadcasting example) are all rendered correctly, and informal "ти" holds. The defects are surface-level. (1) "quasi-probability" is misspelled as «квазійовірнісн-/квазійовірності» (missing м) at 4 places — lines 123, 223, 917, 979; the rest of the uk corpus uses the correct «квазіймовірнісн-», so this file is the sole outlier. (2) Line 30 has a gender-agreement error, «задавати один схему» instead of «одну схему». (3) Line 122 coins the hybrid «поshot-вимірювання» (Cyrillic prefix glued to Latin "shot") for "per-shot measurements" — a native writer would write «вимірювання для кожного shot». (4) Line 126 calques "in terms of" as «організують дані у термінах імен класичних регістрів» (natural: «за іменами…»), and lines 780/1140 use the reflexive «блок коду повернеться з помилкою» where «поверне помилку» is required. (5) Line 80 drops the modality of "which can be multiple observables and parameters", stating flatly «— кілька спостережуваних і параметрів».

examples.source: Each PUB is a tuple that contains one circuit and the data broadcasted to that circuit, which can be multiple observables and parameters.
examples.suggested: …та дані, що транслюються на цю схему, — це можуть бути кілька спостережуваних і параметрів.

examples.why: The English "can be" is possibility; the dash construction asserts the data IS multiple observables and parameters. A dropped qualifier rather than a changed fact, but it slightly over-specifies what a PUB must contain.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inverted conditions, swapped quantities or hallucinated claims — and core terminology is correct and consistent (карта ознак, методи ядра / матриця ядра, навчання з учителем / без учителя, скалярний добуток, заплутаність, кубіт, деквантизація), with informal "ти" held everywhere (заповни, зверни увагу, дай відповідь, натисни). What a native technical editor would still change is a cluster of calques: the repeated adverbial "відомо" construction ("відомо класично складна", "відомо придатний", "алгоритм Шора відомо розв'язує" — should be "як відомо, розв'язує"), "успіх класифікації є надійним до реальних міркувань" for "robust to real-world considerations" (стійким до реальних чинників), "кінцева похибка вибірки" which mis-parses "finite sampling error" (finite modifies sampling: "похибка скінченної вибірки"), "неадекватне" as a false friend for "inadequate" (недостатнє), and the non-standard verb form "як ми поясним" (пояснимо). The Dequantization definition is compressed — "класичним, який виконує схожі завдання з подібним масштабуванням" says the classical algorithm performs *similar tasks*, where the English says it *performs similarly* on a given set of tasks; the concept still survives via "лише поліноміально повільнішим" in the next sentence, so this blurs rather than misleads. Smaller items: labels rendered as "марковані" then "позначені" in the same paragraph, "augment or complement" flattened to just "доповнювати", the closing "See the quiz for further details." dropped, an added UI sentence before the last check-in ("Прочитай питання нижче... натисни трикутник"), and "Танг відкрив" (Ewin Tang is female → "відкрила").

examples.translation: задача класифікації була ретельно вибрана … як (1) відомо класично складна … алгоритм Шора відомо розв'язує задачу дискретного логарифму за поліноміальний час
examples.why: "відомо" is used three times as a bare pre-modifier (also "відомо придатний"), which is ungrammatical calqued English syntax; a Ukrainian technical writer would use the parenthetical "як відомо".

examples.source: the data to be classified are separated by a wide margin using the quantum algorithm, such that the classification success is robust to real-world considerations like finite sampling error
examples.suggested: дані розділені широким зазором (маржею) …, тому класифікація залишається стійкою до реальних чинників, таких як похибка скінченної вибірки
examples.translation: дані для класифікації розділені широким полем при використанні квантового алгоритму, тому успіх класифікації є надійним до реальних міркувань, таких як кінцева похибка вибірки
examples.why: Three slips in one sentence: SVM "margin" as "поле"; "robust to" calqued as "надійним до" (correct is "стійким до"); and "finite sampling error" re-bracketed as "кінцева похибка вибірки", attaching *finite* to the error instead of to the sampling.

examples.source: Dequantization refers to the replacement of a given quantum algorithm with a classical one that performs similarly to a quantum algorithm for a given set of tasks, typically including scaling.
examples.suggested: Деквантизація — це заміна квантового алгоритму класичним, який на певному наборі задач працює подібно до квантового, зокрема й за масштабуванням.
examples.translation: Деквантизація — це заміна квантового алгоритму класичним, який виконує схожі завдання з подібним масштабуванням.
examples.why: "виконує схожі завдання" shifts the criterion from *comparable performance on the same tasks* to *doing similar tasks*; the defining property of dequantization is the performance/scaling match, not task similarity.

examples.source: This is a true statement, but it is inadequate, and a bit misleading as we will explain.

examples.why: "неадекватне" is a false friend for "inadequate" (in Ukrainian it reads as "inappropriate/unhinged"), and "поясним" is a non-standard form of "пояснимо".

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inverted conditions, no swapped quantities, no hallucinated claims; informal "ти" holds consistently ("Зверни увагу", "Встанови його", "Ти можеш експортувати", "Дізнайся", "дивись"). Two editorial defects: (1) the "Наступні кроки" Admonition contains a leftover untranslated English bullet "- Visit the [Verify your program](/guides/debugging-tools) topic." immediately followed by its Ukrainian translation "- Відвідай тему [Перевір свою програму](./debugging-tools)." — the same recommendation is rendered twice, once in English, and the stray line is also un-indented relative to the neighbouring bullets. Neither would teach a learner something false, so this stays MINOR.

examples.source: Note these tools are still in an exploratory phase of development and will continue to evolve as Qiskit's support for dynamic circuit capabilities expressed by OpenQASM 3 increases.
examples.suggested: Зверни увагу, що ці інструменти ще перебувають на дослідницькому етапі розробки і розвиватимуться в міру того, як у Qiskit зростатиме підтримка можливостей динамічних схем, які виражає OpenQASM 3.
examples.translation: Зверни увагу, що ці інструменти ще перебувають на дослідницькому етапі розробки і продовжуватимуть розвиватися разом із підтримкою можливостей динамічних схем, які виражає OpenQASM 3 у Qiskit.
examples.why: "у Qiskit" is stranded at the end and reads as modifying what OpenQASM 3 expresses rather than where the support lives; the English "as ... increases" (a growing-support condition) flattens into a vague "разом із підтримкою". Calqued word order a native technical writer would recast.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: every claim tracks the English, including the tricky ones (little-endian ordering, CNOT flips qubit 1 only if qubit 0 is |1⟩, the "superposition is a mathematical description, not a testable physical fact" caveat, and the "measuring one instantly affects the probabilities for the other" phrasing that avoids over-claiming). Core terminology is correct and consistent throughout — вентиль (gate), кубіт, заплутаність, суперпозиція, спостережувана (observable), константа нормування, власні стани (eigenstates) — and informal "ти" holds with no Ви/Ваш slips. What a native technical editor would change is wording, not meaning: "Два члени кожен представляють два можливі результати" (line 51) is a word-order calque of "The two terms each represent…"; "трьома різними вибірками базисів" (line 168) uses вибірка = statistical *sample* where "вибір/варіант базису" is meant; and in the interference paragraph "як накладні хвилі, які можуть підсилювати або скасовувати одна одну" (line 271) uses накладний = "overhead/attached (invoice)" and скасовувати = "cancel (an appointment)" instead of the physics idiom (хвилі, що накладаються / гасити одна одну), with "шаблони результатів вимірювань" for "patterns" in the same sentence (шаблон = template; закономірності fits). Two smaller stiff spots: "звичайне вимірювання виконує роботу" (line 192, literal "does the job") and "твоя схема виробляє бажаний стан" (line 342, виробляє = manufactures; створює/дає is natural).

examples.why: Literal rendering of the English idiom "does the job"; «виконує роботу» reads as unfinished machine output rather than a technical writer's sentence.

examples.translation: підтверди, що твоя схема виробляє бажаний стан
examples.why: «виробляє» carries a manufacturing sense; a physicist writing in Ukrainian would use створює/дає for producing a quantum state.

editor_note: No misleading drift: statuses, the 16 CPU / 32 GB figure, the 1024-byte arithmetic, the flat-`/data` limitation and the `tar`/`h5` restriction are all faithful, and informal "ти" holds throughout ("Якщо ти читаєш", "Переконайся", "твоїх програм"). Four editor-level slips remain. (1) In the closing paragraph "for consistent and flexible data management" becomes "для зручного та гнучкого керування даними" — "consistent" (узгодженого/послідовного) is replaced by "зручного" (convenient), swapping the claim being made about the API. (2) The named concept "quantum-centric supercomputing" is rendered as the hardware plural "квантово-центричні суперкомп'ютери" instead of "квантово-центричні суперобчислення". (3) "data resources" is rendered as "інформаційними ресурсами" in the title/description/intro but as "даними" in the body heading "Керування даними у програмі" — an in-file split, and "інформаційні ресурси" is the weaker choice. (4) Minor translationese: "воркер-таск" (line ~128) is a raw double calque, and the title uses "Керування" while the description uses "Управління".

examples.translation: `file_upload()`, `file_download()` та `file_delete()` можна викликати як із локального експерименту, так і з завантаженої програми — для зручного та гнучкого керування даними.
examples.why: "consistent" is the point of the sentence (the same API works identically from either context); rendering it as "зручного" (convenient) substitutes a different, weaker claim.

examples.why: "воркер-таск" transliterates both halves of the English compound; a Ukrainian technical writer would write "завдання воркера" (or "робоче завдання") rather than stacking two calques.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the promise, the two cases (one-to-one vs two-to-one), the p(y) case split, the null-space/Gaussian-elimination post-processing and the 2^{n/2-1}-1 classical lower bound all survive intact, and the informal "ми"-register holds with no Ви/Вам slips. What a native editor would still change: (1) "phase kickback" is rendered "фазове відлуння" ("phase echo") whereas the rest of the uk corpus uses "фазовий відкат" (5 hits) — imprecise and inconsistent across files; (2) the Deutsch-Jozsa name is transliterated "Дойча-Жожа" three times, against the corpus-dominant "Дойча-Йожи" (42 hits); (3) a gender-agreement typo "Цю позначення" (should be "Це позначення") and the Russianism "Це вірно" (native: "Це справедливо"); (4) two small softenings — "if we run the circuit sufficiently many times" is dropped from the statistical-evidence sentence, and "There's nothing special about this particular number" becomes "Це не унікальне значення". None of these would lead a learner to a false belief.

examples.source: but this time there's no phase kickback; the bottom $m$ qubits all go into the query gate in the state $\vert 0\rangle.$
examples.suggested: але цього разу немає фазового відкату; ...
examples.translation: але цього разу немає фазового відлуння; нижні $m$ кубітів входять у вентиль запиту в стані $\vert 0\rangle.$
examples.why: «відлуння» means 'echo'; the established rendering of phase kickback in the uk corpus is «фазовий відкат» (5 occurrences elsewhere). Recognizable but imprecise and inconsistent across the course.

examples.source: the Deutsch-Jozsa and Bernstein-Vazirani problems
examples.suggested: задачі Дойча-Йожи та Бернштейна-Вазірані
examples.translation: задачі Дойча-Жожа та Бернштейна-Вазірані
examples.why: Jozsa is transliterated «Жожа» here (3×) but «Йожи/Йожі» in 44 other uk files. Consistent within the file, so the learner can still identify the algorithm, but it is the wrong spelling of the name.

examples.source: (This notation should not be confused with the *inverse* of the function $f,$ which may not exist.
examples.suggested: (Це позначення не слід плутати з *оберненою функцією* $f,$ ...
examples.translation: (Цю позначення не слід плутати з *оберненою функцією* $f,$ яка може не існувати.
examples.why: Gender/case agreement error: «позначення» is neuter, so «Цю» is ungrammatical — a native writer would write «Це позначення».

examples.source: we can use that evidence to find $s$ with very high probability if we run the circuit sufficiently many times.
examples.suggested: ...щоб знайти $s$ із дуже великою ймовірністю, якщо запустимо схему достатню кількість разів.
examples.translation: і ми можемо скористатися ними, щоб знайти $s$ із дуже великою ймовірністю.
examples.why: The conditional qualifier 'if we run the circuit sufficiently many times' is dropped, making the guarantee read as unconditional. Not misleading in context (the next paragraph immediately fixes k = n + 10), but the caveat should be restored.

examples.source: At this point, the analysis diverges from the ones for the previous algorithms in this lesson.
examples.suggested: На цьому етапі аналіз відрізняється від аналізів попередніх алгоритмів цього уроку.
examples.translation: На цьому місці аналіз відхиляється від попередніх алгоритмів.
examples.why: «На цьому місці» is a calque of 'at this point'; and the sentence literally says the analysis diverges from the algorithms rather than from their analyses. 'in this lesson' is also dropped.

examples.source: This is true in both the case that $s = 0^n$ and $s\neq 0^n.$
examples.suggested: Це справедливо як у випадку $s = 0^n,$ так і в разі $s\neq 0^n.$
examples.translation: Це вірно як у випадку $s = 0^n,$ так і в разі $s\neq 0^n.$
examples.why: «вірно» in the sense of 'true/valid' is a Russianism; Ukrainian mathematical prose uses «справедливо» or «правильно».

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout and terminology is correct and consistent (схема for circuit, рендерер for renderer, вивід for output, kwarg/backend kept in English, informal "ти" held everywhere) — nothing here would teach a false concept. Three editorial slips: the hedge "appear to have the same effect" is flattened to a flat assertion "вони мають однаковий ефект", which drops precisely the nuance that `print` and `draw` only *look* equivalent inside Jupyter; "Drawing a large-scale circuit inline in a Jupyter notebook" loses "inline", so the sentence no longer explains *why* it is slow (rendering in the notebook itself rather than to a file); and "замість як методу об'єкта схеми" is an ungrammatical calque of "instead of as a method of", where a native writer would write "а не як метод об'єкта схеми". None of these invert a condition or a quantity, so this stays MINOR.

examples.source: Since Jupyter notebooks display the output of the last line of each cell, they appear to have the same effect.
examples.suggested: Оскільки Jupyter notebooks відображають вивід останнього рядка кожної комірки, здається, що вони мають однаковий ефект.
examples.translation: Оскільки Jupyter notebooks відображають вивід останнього рядка кожної комірки, вони мають однаковий ефект.
examples.why: The hedge "appear to" is the hinge of the sentence: the preceding sentence has just established that print and draw genuinely differ (None + side effect vs. returned object). Dropping it turns an "it only looks the same" observation into a flat claim of equivalence, weakening the very distinction the paragraph exists to teach.

examples.source: Drawing a large-scale circuit inline in a Jupyter notebook can be slow or unreadable.
examples.suggested: Малювання великої схеми безпосередньо в Jupyter notebook може бути повільним або нечитабельним.
examples.translation: Малювання великої схеми в Jupyter notebook може бути повільним або нечитабельним.
examples.why: "inline" is dropped, so the contrast with the very next sentence (save to a file instead) loses its footing — the reader no longer sees that it is the in-notebook rendering, not circuit drawing as such, that is the problem.

examples.source: …you prefer to draw a circuit with a self-contained function instead of as a method of a circuit object…
examples.suggested: …ти віддаєш перевагу малювати схему окремою самостійною функцією, а не методом об'єкта схеми…
examples.translation: …ти віддаєш перевагу малюванню схеми за допомогою самостійної функції замість як методу об'єкта схеми…
examples.why: "замість як методу" is a word-for-word calque of English "instead of as a method" that is not grammatical Ukrainian; a native technical writer would use the contrastive "а не" construction.

editor_note: Semantically faithful throughout — I checked every negation, quantifier and iff-claim (the «$P\geq 0$ *не* означає, що кожен елемент $P$ є невід'ємним» caveat, the "one eigenvalue equal to 1, all others 0" statement, the global-phase degeneracy paragraph and the final "тоді й лише тоді" faithfulness claim) and found no drift, no dropped caveat and no hallucinated sentence; informal "ти" holds («Зверни увагу»), and «faithful representation → точне представлення» is the correct domain convention. The defects are cosmetic. (1) The core term "trace" is split within the file: condition 1 is titled «Одинична слідова сума» — a non-standard coinage — while the very next section and all following prose correctly use «слід» / «Слід матриці»; the conventional rendering of "unit trace" is «Одиничний слід». (2) In the diagonal-entries bullet, "weight" or "likelihood" both collapse onto probability-words — «вагу» або «ймовірність» — right after the same sentence already said «дають нам ймовірності», so the English's deliberately looser second gloss flattens into a tautology. (3) «lowercase» is dropped from "The lowercase Greek letter ρ" → «Грецька літера ρ». (4) The connector `\quad\text{and}\quad` between the four example matrices is still English "and" while the surrounding prose is Ukrainian.

examples.source: 1. Unit trace: $\operatorname{Tr}(\rho) = 1.$
examples.suggested: 1. Одиничний слід: $\operatorname{Tr}(\rho) = 1.$
examples.translation: 1. Одинична слідова сума: $\operatorname{Tr}(\rho) = 1.$
examples.why: «слідова сума» is a non-standard coinage and is inconsistent with the section heading «Слід матриці» (line 52) and every later use of «слід» — the same concept is named two ways within the file. Not misleading (the trace IS the sum of the diagonal), so MINOR.

examples.source: so we can think about these entries as describing the "weight" or "likelihood" associated with each classical state
examples.suggested: …як про «вагу» або «правдоподібність» (шанс), пов'язану з кожним класичним станом
examples.translation: тому можна думати про ці елементи як про «вагу» або «ймовірність», пов'язану з кожним класичним станом
examples.why: The same sentence already stated «дають нам ймовірності появи кожного класичного стану», so rendering the informal gloss "likelihood" as «ймовірність» makes the second half circular; English deliberately offers a looser, non-technical synonym pair.

examples.source: The lowercase Greek letter $\rho$ is a conventional first choice for the name of a density matrix
examples.suggested: Мала грецька літера $\rho$ — традиційний перший вибір…
examples.translation: Грецька літера $\rho$ — традиційний перший вибір для назви матриці густини
examples.why: The qualifier "lowercase" is dropped. Harmless here (the symbol is shown), but it is a dropped modifier a native technical editor would restore, especially since uppercase Greek letters name other objects later in the course.

examples.source: \quad\text{and}\quad
examples.suggested: \quad\text{і}\quad
examples.translation: \quad\text{and}\quad
examples.why: Prose word inside \text{} renders visibly as English "and" between the four example density matrices, in an otherwise fully Ukrainian paragraph.
